an early draft would give; the fourth confuses the participant instrument,
which is a paced emitter and a label source, with an access point.
cards.question:
A committee member asks what AP stands for and whether your access points are
dual-band. What is the correct answer?
cards.title: The trap in the list

cards.back:
Wi-Fi CSI can count people, but every deployed model decays: the
count→signal mechanism is universal (positive rank correlation in 7/7
real environments), while the absolute mapping is environment- and
hardware-specific and drifts. My contribution is (1) a four-pillar formal
theory explaining and predicting this — partial-pooling calibration,
a derived concave scattering law, state-space fusion, spectral counting +
submodular placement; (2) a BLE-calibrated architecture where cheap
continuous BLE monitoring triggers periodic recalibration campaigns;
(3) an evidence programme — reproducible campaigns, real-data
validations, a pre-registered hardware protocol, and a deployed Pi5/AX210
capture fleet.
cards.front: "Summarise your contribution in two minutes."
cards.title: The elevator pitch

cards.back:
Occupancy is the master variable for building energy, safety, and space
operations, and cameras fail exactly where deployment happens: privacy
law and acceptance, lighting, occlusion, cost of coverage. RF sensing
reuses existing infrastructure and counts WITHOUT identifying. The open
problem is not detection — it is keeping calibrated accuracy over months
without labelled data, which is precisely what the thesis addresses.
cards.front: "Why is crowd counting worth a doctorate? Cameras exist."
cards.title: Why does this matter

cards.back:
BLE is already carried by occupants and installed as infrastructure; it
gives a coarse count without identity; narrowband RSSI at many anchors is
measurably better at location fingerprinting than sparse wideband CSI
links (2.49×); and it drifts DIFFERENTLY from CSI, which is what makes
the cross-modal disagreement statistic informative. Its sufficiency as
ground truth is itself a stated, gated hypothesis — not an assumption.
cards.front: "Why BLE as the calibration side-channel and not another sensor?"
cards.title: Why BLE

cards.back:
Real-data accuracy claims currently ride on public datasets, so
cross-dataset confounds remain until first-party capture closes the
loop; the flagship calibration hypothesis is still plausible, not
supported — no public dataset has synchronized BLE + CSI + counts, which
is exactly why the IP-106 protocol and the AX210 fleet exist. I state
this before the committee does.
cards.front: "What is the biggest threat to the validity of your results?"
cards.title: Biggest weakness

cards.back:
Each hypothesis carries an explicit defeater and gate. Flagship: if the
IP-106 multi-week two-site study shows periodic BLE recalibration does
not outperform one-shot calibration (or BLE-vs-headcount R² < 0.7, so
the ground truth itself fails), the architecture claim falls. The
portfolio already contains executed refutations — continuity prior,
topology fingerprint — showing the machinery falsifies for real.
cards.front: "What result would falsify your central claim?"
cards.title: What would change your mind

cards.back:
Three things: (1) the calibration plane is FORMALISED — partial pooling
with platform nesting, where the measured 42% two-anchor recovery is
reproduced as empirical-Bayes shrinkage, and placement becomes
Bayesian-optimal design; (2) the trigger is cross-MODAL — an independent
cheap modality detects drift where self-monitoring provably false-alarms
(17%); (3) the economics are stated honestly as condition-based
maintenance: parity at ¼ spend, not accuracy magic. Novelty is anchored
per-hypothesis against named prior art in the frontmatter.
cards.front: "Recalibration for drifting sensors is old news. What is new?"
cards.title: Novelty interrogation

cards.back:
Because transfer is the problem, not fit: learned fingerprints break
under layout change (feature-type result, ratio 0.076) and synthetic
training data over-codes environment (0.99 vs 0.83, unclosable by
impairments). A physically derived low-dimensional observable —
amplitude variance with a concave law — travels across 7 environments
and stays interpretable enough to calibrate with 2 anchors. Deep models
can sit on top later; the calibration theory is what makes ANY estimator
deployable.
cards.front: "Why calibrated classical features instead of end-to-end deep learning?"
cards.title: Deep-learning challenge

cards.back:
Real: 7-env LOEO (0.72/1.32/1.75/2.07 ladder, 42%), OPERAnet MI 0.174
in-band, WiMANS dual-band re-analysis (0.71/0.28), scattering-law fits
(5/7, 3/3), first AX210 link measurements. In-silico: filter numbers
(0.53, ρ 0.97), material-drift 74%, observability paradox, anchor-
placement recovery, all fingerprint ladders. I keep the two lists
separate in every chapter — sim informs structure, real data carries
accuracy.
cards.front:
"Which of your numbers would you defend as REAL evidence, and which are
simulation?"
cards.title: Sim/real division

cards.back:
The architecture is designed for estates: hierarchical calibration
shares statistical strength across zones (new zones start at the nested
prior, 1.49 not 1.97); the trigger allocates a fixed calibration budget
to the zones that drift (¼-spend parity measured on a 4-zone estate);
placement is submodular so greedy planning is near-optimal per floor.
Saturation is the physical limit — the concave law says marginal count
information vanishes in dense hubs, so I claim counting bands, not
unbounded N.
cards.front: "Does this scale beyond one room — a mall, a campus?"
cards.title: Scaling question

cards.back:
The design goal is count-without-identify: CSI features are aggregate
channel statistics, not tracks or identities; BLE is used for coarse
presence counts, not device-level trajectories, and the ground-truth
protocol runs under institutional consent in staged spaces. RF counting
is the privacy-PRESERVING alternative to cameras (rusca2024), and
802.11bf standardisation is bringing exactly this sensing into every AP
— better to build its calibration theory with privacy as a constraint.
cards.front: "You are sensing people who did not consent. Ethics?"
cards.title: Privacy and ethics

cards.back:
Because the calibration hypotheses need synchronized BLE + CSI + counts
over weeks — no public dataset has it. Commodity extraction stacks were
x86/legacy-NIC bound; the AX210-on-Pi5 port plus our csid daemon gives a
14-node, thermally characterised, remotely operated fleet with a
self-describing capture format — and building it surfaced silent bugs
(chain-major layout, imag-first I/Q) that would have corrupted every
phase analysis downstream.
cards.front: "Why build your own capture hardware instead of using existing tools?"
cards.title: Why a fleet

cards.back:
The hardware evidence legs: IP-106 staged-room captures (calibration
regimes, drift horizons), the seated-crowd spectral leg, and the
low-density phasor-scaling leg — each pre-registered with locked
analyses. Theory and writing are ahead of the data: four pillars are
threaded through the chapters, two already real-data supported. The
thesis stands on the theory + existing real validations; the fleet turns
supported into strong.
cards.front: "What remains between today and a defended thesis?"
cards.title: Timeline

cards.back:
A SELF-LABELLING reference: an independent source of occupancy ground truth
that can re-anchor the estimator when its environment changes, without an
engineer collecting labels.
cards.front:
In one sentence, what does CSI counting most need that it cannot supply
itself?
cards.title: Why CSI needs a partner at all
cards.why:
The CSI chapter established the need structurally — environmental
sensitivity, hardware heterogeneity, multi-person ambiguity — and
deliberately left the case for BLE to be earned here rather than assumed
there.

cards.back:
The log-distance path-loss model: received level falls as ten times the
path-loss exponent times the log of distance over a reference distance,
plus a zero-mean Gaussian shadowing term. The exponent n is the
per-environment parameter.
cards.front:
Write the model behind BLE ranging and name the parameter that must be
calibrated per environment.
cards.title: The range primitive
cards.why:
It is not universal. Fitted exponents run from 2 in free space to above 4
in cluttered indoor spaces, varying with building materials, furniture and
obstruction. Anyone quoting a single indoor exponent is quoting one
building.

choices: Because BLE advertises on three channels and they have different transmit powers.
Because the actual received power is the superposition of numerous reflected, diffracted and shadowed components, while the path-loss model assumes only distance-dependent mean attenuation.
Because address randomisation prevents associating consecutive readings with one device.
Because the receiver's automatic gain control has not settled.
cards.explanation:
Multipath causes rapid fluctuation across small displacements, potentially
spanning tens of decibels, and human bodies at 2.4 GHz add attenuation
varying with posture and orientation. The model assumes a mean; the
measurement is a superposition. Without statistical correction — temporal
averaging, filtering, or weighted least-squares that down-weights
high-variance measurements — raw multilateration yields errors of several
metres. Randomisation is a real problem in this chapter, but it bounds
identifier-to-device counting, not ranging.
cards.question: Why is one instantaneous BLE RSSI reading a poor proxy for distance?
cards.title: Why a single reading is useless

cards.back:
A metre-grade BLE position may GATE which link's sensitive region a body
occupies. It can NEVER predict per-zone phase.
cards.front: The thesis bounds what a BLE position can be used for. State the bound.
cards.title: What BLE position is allowed to be used for
cards.why:
The bound comes from the thesis's own Fresnel-geometry analysis, not from
caution. It is what keeps the positional leg of the campaign honest: the
census leg is the load-bearing one, because the calibration architecture
consumes COUNTS, not positions.

cards.back:
It bounds how well an IDENTIFIER count approximates a DEVICE count — one
phone rotating its address becomes several pseudonyms, inflating the tally.
cards.front: What does MAC-address randomisation bound, and what does it NOT bound?
cards.title: The privacy floor
cards.why:
It says nothing about the larger and more awkward gap: a device count is
not a headcount at all. Keeping those two conversions separate — identifier
to device, device to person — is what stops a single fudge factor from
absorbing both.

choices: Because the published figures come from offices rather than libraries.

Two objections: the factor is not stationary — it varies by hour, by day, and more sharply across crowd TYPES — and a point correction converts an unknown bias into a confident number, moving the estimate without widening it.
Because the conversion is not identifiable from a device count alone.
Because randomisation already inflates the identifier count by a similar factor, so the two cancel.
cards.explanation:
The second objection is the more basic one, and it is the one that connects
to the output contract. Moving an estimate without widening it is precisely
the wrong response to not knowing something. A commuter flow, a lecture
cohort and an exam hall differ in carriage in ways no single scalar spans —
so importing one is not conservative, it is confidently wrong in an unknown
direction.
cards.question:
Camera-labelled building studies report device-to-occupant ratios near 1.2.
Why does the thesis refuse to just multiply by one?
cards.title: The rejected remedy

cards.back:
Two observations of ONE occupancy state with DISJOINT NUISANCE STRUCTURES
determine both the count and the device-to-person ratio, where either alone
leaves them confounded.
cards.front:
State the identification argument in one sentence, and name the property
that makes it work.
cards.title: The joint identification argument
cards.why:
Disjointness is the property. CSI perturbation responds to bodies,
device-free, indifferent to what those bodies carry; device activity
responds to radios and is indifferent to whether they move. The asymmetry
has been treated throughout the literature as the weakness of each. Read
jointly it is an asset.

cards.back:
It is PROPAGATED, not corrected — it widens the predictive distribution
rather than displacing a point estimate.
cards.front:
What happens to the residual uncertainty in the ratio, and why is that the
right treatment?
cards.title: Propagate, do not correct
cards.why:
So a count that is uncertain because the crowd is unusual is REPORTED as
uncertain. That is behaviour a deployment can act on, and it is behaviour a
scalar correction cannot express. It is also why the output contract had to
be fixed before this chapter: propagation needs somewhere to propagate to.

cards.back:
First, where the joint fit is under-determined the ratio is recoverable
without labels from the deployment's own statistics: stationary devices —
printers, access points, the instrument's own management radios — are
strippable against an empty window. Second, the participant instrument
supplies windows with a KNOWN headcount, making the ratio measured on this
deployment rather than imported.
cards.front:
Name the two fallbacks behind the joint fit, and say why they are stated at
all.
cards.title: The two fallbacks
cards.why:
They are stated because the architecture should not depend on its most
ambitious layer succeeding. This testbed is also better placed than the
office-building precedents for the subtraction, because its empty window is
CERTIFIED rather than presumed.

cards.back:
The transmitter CENSUS recorded with every frame; the DELIVERY DEFICIT of a
paced reference against a same-night control on the other band; and the
ADVERTISEMENT stream. It costs no hardware — all three are already in
every capture the project has taken.
cards.front:
What are the three observables of the device-activity channel, and what
does it cost?
cards.title: The second count channel
cards.why:
Its failure modes are approximately orthogonal to CSI's: CSI counts bodies
through motion and cannot distinguish a still crowd from an empty room,
whereas device activity counts radios and is indifferent to motion.

choices: Into 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz emitters, because only one band carries clients.
Into fleet management radios, infrastructure, and locally-administered addresses — only the third tracks people, and pooling them inflates the count with the instrument's own traffic.
Into strong and weak emitters, since only nearby devices are people.
Into randomised and stable addresses, since only stable ones can be counted reliably.
cards.explanation:
The separation changes the answer entirely. Our own nodes are loud — one
appears as comfortably the loudest emitter in the room. Infrastructure
includes access points advertising several networks from sequential
addresses on one organisational prefix. Only addresses carrying the
locally-administered bit that phones and laptops set when they randomise
track people. Note the inversion in the fourth option: randomised addresses
are the ones that MATTER here, not the ones to discard.
cards.question:
The transmitter census is only meaningful once addresses are separated.
Into what, and why does it change the answer?
cards.title: Three populations, one census

cards.back:
Over more than a thousand minutes of certified-empty observation the
distinct client-address count is ZERO — not small, zero. The control:
infrastructure addresses were captured during EVERY certified-empty hour,
demonstrating the receiver was pulling CSI out of ambient frames throughout
and simply saw no client devices.
cards.front:
State the measured floor of the device-activity channel and the control
that makes it interpretable.
cards.title: The floor, and the control that makes it a measurement
cards.why:
Without that control the zero would be indistinguishable from a dead
receive path. With it, the detection threshold is trivially one randomised
client address — there is no floor to clear.

cards.back:
It is a ONE-CLASS result. There is a rigorous null and NO SENSITIVITY
ESTIMATE whatsoever, so nothing in it speaks to whether the census scales
with the number of people present.
cards.front: The chapter is blunt about the census's limitation. What is it?
cards.title: What the census does NOT establish
cards.why:
The daytime peak observed — a handful of distinct clients — is almost
certainly a single human being: an operator laptop holding sessions to ten
nodes transmits far more than a pocketed phone, and one phone rotating its
address becomes several pseudonyms. The occupancy ramp is designed to
answer exactly this.

choices: Density — BLE is reliable when sparse, CSI at moderate density.
TIME AND OBSERVABILITY — BLE is an intermittent drift-free absolute whose error is a census bias; CSI is a continuous relative whose calibration decays with elapsed time.
Frequency — BLE occupies 2.4 GHz and CSI 5 GHz, so they see different multipath.
Spatial resolution — BLE resolves zones, CSI resolves links.
cards.explanation:
The first option is the RETIRED formulation and it is included because it
was in an earlier draft of this thesis. It was retired for two measured
reasons: the coupled simulation found one modality dominant at EVERY
density while only the staleness switch tracked the error envelope, and the
graded BLE-RSSI density signal the density axis presumed was independently
refuted. The consequence is that the fused estimator is a confidence-weighted
switch on anchor FRESHNESS, not a blend gated on density.
cards.question: On what axis are BLE and CSI complementary?
cards.title: The complementarity axis

cards.back:
In the static-placement regime that proxies a seated crowd — precisely
where the temporal CSI feature collapses toward the fading floor — the BLE
anchor still separates an occupied room from an empty one with a large
effect size, holding up even under substantial simulated advertisement
noise.
cards.front:
A co-registered ray-tracing study gives in-silico support for one half of
the complementarity. Which half, and what does the anchor NOT do?
cards.title: What the co-registered study supports
cards.why:
But its blockage response SATURATES after the first occupants, so in that
layout it resolves occupancy PRESENCE rather than graded headcount. Two
caveats bound it: the BLE measurement noise is a self-authored model, so
this motivates the anchor's role rather than guaranteeing accuracy; and the
penetration-ratio stability the calibration argument rests on is a property
of real device populations.

cards.back:
Nobody measures the FRESHNESS-STRATIFIED error interaction — how the two
modalities' errors relate as a function of how stale the anchor is.
cards.front:
The complementarity claim ends by naming a gap in the whole literature.
What is it?
cards.title: What no published study measures
cards.why:
Establishing it on hardware is the drift-study leg of the pre-registered
campaign. A claim that identifies a gap AND owns the instrument that could
close it is in a much stronger position than one that merely notes an
absence.

cards.back:
BLE RSSI noise propagates through the per-environment path-loss model to a
per-device distance variance, which maps to a count-domain standard
deviation via the occupancy model's Jacobian. τ is a chosen multiple of
that propagated uncertainty.
cards.front: How is the recalibration threshold τ derived, rather than tuned?
cards.title: The trigger threshold
cards.why:
So only drift exceeding the NOISE FLOOR OF THE REFERENCE ITSELF fires a
campaign. A threshold picked by hand would be arbitrary; a threshold
derived from the reference's own noise is defensible in one sentence. A
hysteresis condition — exceedance persisting across two consecutive
campaigns — bounds the false-trigger rate on top.

cards.back:
The per-subcarrier complex channel frequency response a commodity OFDM
receiver estimates during demodulation. Under the narrowband model
Y(k) = H(k)X(k) + N(k), CSI is the vector of recovered H(k) over the
occupied subcarriers. In MIMO it becomes a tensor indexed by
transmit–receive antenna pair, each entry decomposing into an amplitude and
a phase.
cards.front: Define CSI precisely enough that a sceptic cannot accuse you of hand-waving.
cards.title: What CSI is
cards.why:
Two consequences follow immediately: the channel is sampled at subcarrier
granularity rather than as an aggregate, so it RESOLVES frequency-selective
fading that scalar power collapses; and the receiver had to compute it
anyway, which is what makes the modality free.

cards.back:
Because each subcarrier effectively probes the environment at a slightly
different wavelength, even a small positional change or a single added
occupant alters the interference pattern in a SUBCARRIER-DEPENDENT manner
that a single power reading cannot resolve.
cards.front:
Why does subcarrier resolution matter physically, rather than just giving
more numbers?
cards.title: Why subcarriers matter
cards.why:
A body's effect is frequency-selective. Wideband averaging suppresses
exactly that structure into noise, which is the one-sentence reason RSSI
loses the signal rather than merely reporting it coarsely.

cards.back:
Carrier frequency offset and sampling frequency offset from mismatched
oscillators and clocks; symbol timing offset and packet detection delay,
which inject linear phase ramps as the FFT window mis-aligns; cyclic shift
diversity and residual random phase rotations.
cards.front:
Name the impairments that make raw CSI phase unusable, and say why
isolating the channel is non-trivial.
cards.title: The impairment stack
cards.why:
They are not constant — they vary packet to packet. The desired signal and
the contamination occupy the same measurement, which is why sanitisation is
an estimation problem rather than a subtraction of a known bias.

choices: One works on amplitude, the other on phase.
One DIFFERENCES across antennas or subcarriers so common-mode terms cancel; the other FITS AND SUBTRACTS the subcarrier-linear phase slope that timing and sampling offsets produce.
One is applied at capture time, the other offline.
One requires a reference transmitter, the other does not.
cards.explanation:
Both target phase and both are offline. The differencing family exploits
the fact that several distortions are common across the receiver's RF
front end and cancel under subtraction. The line-fitting family exploits
the fact that sampling and timing offsets manifest as a subcarrier-LINEAR
slope, so unwrapping and subtracting a fitted line removes them. Newer work
casts sanitisation as a deterministic projection onto a device-agnostic
canonical grid — the same principle throughout: estimate and strip the
instrument so what remains reflects the room.
cards.question: Two remedies dominate CSI sanitisation. What distinguishes them?
cards.title: The two sanitisation families

cards.back:
It divides the CSI of one antenna by that of a co-located antenna on the
same RF chain. Both see the same carrier-frequency offset, sampling-frequency
offset and random phase rotation, so those terms appear identically in
numerator and denominator and cancel arithmetically — no per-offset
estimation step at all.
cards.front: What does the CSI ratio do, and what is its one practical caveat?
cards.title: The CSI ratio, and its failure mode
cards.why:
Denominator-null instability. When the reference antenna's coefficient
passes near zero under deep fading, the ratio AMPLIFIES noise instead of
suppressing it. Implementations pick the strongest receive chain as
denominator and discard or interpolate subcarriers where its magnitude
falls below a threshold.

cards.back:
Multipath enrichment — additional bodies add scattering paths and inflate
the SPREAD of amplitude. And line-of-sight blockage — bodies on the direct
path absorb and diffract, depressing the MEAN amplitude.
cards.front:
Name the two amplitude signatures of crowd occlusion and say what decides
which one carries the count.
cards.title: The two amplitude signatures
cards.why:
Which dominates is governed by the relative strength of the direct path.
Where a strong line of sight exists to be shadowed, mean-amplitude
attenuation dominates; where the channel is already diffuse, variance
statistics dominate. They are geometrically distinct effects, which is why
a practical pipeline retains both feature families.

choices: It was fitted to the data, and the concave form happened to score better.
From the physics: a central-limit argument at low density, plus a finite room whose mutual occlusion caps the number of EFFECTIVE independent scatterers.
From the receiver's automatic gain control compressing large variances.
From the logarithm applied when converting amplitude to decibels.
cards.explanation:
The distinction between derived and fitted is the whole upgrade. Modelling
the channel as a static component plus K independent moving phasors, the
fluctuation power grows with K at low density by a central-limit argument
and saturates as occlusion caps the effective scatterer count — which
yields the exponential-saturation form BEFORE any data is seen. What is
fitted is only the scale. The evidence then confirms the shape rather than
discovering it: the concave form is preferred over a line in most
counting-band environments, and the fitted saturation scale sits inside the
observed occupancy range.
cards.question:
The count-to-variance relation is concave and saturating. Where does the
concavity come from?
cards.title: The derived shape

cards.back:
First, the mean-scaled coefficient of variation is the natural normaliser,
because the static component sets the mean. Second, a shorter wavelength
gives a larger phase swing per unit body displacement, so the 5 GHz
fluctuation feature is more occupancy-discriminative than 2.4 GHz.
cards.front:
The scattering derivation gives two consequences without fitting anything.
Name both.
cards.title: Two free consequences
cards.why:
The band advantage is therefore a PREDICTION of the model, not a separate
empirical fact. That matters at a defense: it converts two findings into
one mechanism, and it means confirming the band advantage confirms the
model rather than adding a coincidence.

cards.back:
At 2.4 GHz, where the variance proxy collapses, the SPECTRAL feature
recovers most of the count signal. So the band advantage is a property of
the FEATURE rather than of the radio.
cards.front:
Pillar 2a corrects the band advantage in a way that matters for deployment.
What is the correction?
cards.title: The correction to the band rule
cards.why:
It matters because much deployed infrastructure has no 5 GHz choice to
make. A design rule that says "use 5 GHz" is useless to a building that
cannot; a rule that says "at 2.4 GHz, change feature" is actionable
everywhere. The conclusion also adds a second qualifier from the corpus:
the measured band advantage is conditional on channel congestion.

cards.back:
A feature extractor feeds two heads — a task head predicting the count, and
a domain classifier trying to identify which room a sample came from. The
two train antagonistically through a gradient-reversal layer, so at
convergence the extractor produces features from which the environment
cannot be recovered but which remain discriminative for the task.
cards.front:
Describe domain-adversarial training in two sentences, and say what it does
NOT tell you.
cards.title: Domain-adversarial training
cards.why:
It treats the environment as a nuisance to be ERASED, and it does not say
which part of the representation was doing the damage. That is the gap the
chapter's own feature-type finding fills — a sharper diagnosis rather than
a better eraser.

choices: The RF modality — CSI is more layout-sensitive than BLE RSSI.
The FEATURE TYPE. Fingerprint features encode the spatial multipath map and fail when it changes; kinematic features encode body dynamics and transfer.
The calibration, which had drifted since training.
The receiver placement, which was optimal for the old layout.
cards.explanation:
This is the reframe that unifies several apparently conflicting reports of
CSI robustness. Per-link absolute CSI amplitude maps and per-link BLE-RSSI
vectors are BOTH fingerprints and both fail; multipath-change rate,
temporal amplitude variance and fading statistics are both kinematic and
both transfer. Sorting by the radio that produced the feature explains
nothing; sorting by feature type explains the whole set. In a paired
rearrangement protocol run in simulation the split replicated in nine of
nine seed pairs, and the lesson is constructive — it says which features a
cross-environment counter should be built from.
cards.question:
A trained RF crowd counter breaks after the furniture is rearranged. On
this thesis's account, what broke?
cards.title: Feature type, not modality

cards.back:
Every environment shows the same monotone occupancy-to-variance RANK
relation, so presence detection transfers cold. But the two platforms
occupy cleanly separated variance bands, so the ABSOLUTE variance-to-count
mapping is device-specific. Holding the platform fixed and swapping the
room costs little; swapping the platform costs a couple of persons.
cards.front:
State the hardware-versus-layout finding precisely: what transfers cold,
what does not, and what follows for the architecture.
cards.title: Hardware over layout
cards.why:
It is the empirical reason the calibration spine must be per DEVICE and not
merely per room — precisely the anchoring role the BLE chapter performs.
It also answers device heterogeneity, which the recent generalisability
survey ranks first among domain-shift factors.

cards.back:
WiFi keystroke inference on a robotic typing platform built specifically to
disentangle sources of domain variation, across a very large controlled
grid of domains. It separates environment-level shift, which is additive
and leaves the target's encoding intact, from encoding-level shift, which
changes the mapping itself — and finds models transfer reliably across the
former and degrade substantially across the latter.
cards.front:
A study of an unrelated task corroborates the hardware-over-layout
ordering. What was the task, and why does the corroboration count for more
than a replication would?
cards.title: The independent corroboration
cards.why:
Different task, different corpus, different failure metric, same ordering.
Two independent literatures converging suggests the finding is a property
of how physical information is ENCODED in a wireless channel, rather than
an artefact of the counting task.

cards.back:
Comparing several domain-adaptation objectives against a model with none,
it finds NO CONSISTENT ADVANTAGE for any of them.
cards.front:
That same corroborating study carries a caution the thesis imports. What is
it?
cards.title: The caution that comes with it
cards.why:
A mechanism labelled "domain adaptation" does not by itself establish that
adaptation is what confers the transfer. Importing an inconvenient finding
from a paper you are otherwise citing approvingly is a strong move at a
defense — it shows the citation was read rather than mined.

choices: Counting needs more labelled examples per class.

Inter-class boundaries in a count regression are ORDINAL and environment-dependent rather than categorically distinct, so the prototypical embedding geometry that makes few-shot classification tractable does not map cleanly onto occupancy levels.
Gestures produce stronger Doppler signatures than crowds.
Counting datasets are smaller.
cards.explanation:
The difficulty is geometric rather than quantitative. Prototypical networks
work by placing well-separated class prototypes in an embedding; "four
people" and "five people" are neighbouring points on an ordinal scale whose
spacing itself shifts between environments. The chapter is also honest that
rigorous few-shot COUNTING benchmarks analogous to those for activity
recognition remain scarce, so this is an argued structural difference plus
an absence of evidence, not a measured comparison.
cards.question:
Few-shot methods reach high accuracy on gesture recognition. Why does the
chapter say counting is structurally harder?
cards.title: Why counting is harder than gestures

cards.back:
Across coupled runs spanning several occupancy levels, two bands and
multiple seeds, the sliding-window temporal coefficient of variation rises
monotonically with occupancy in BOTH bands, while in the settled tail —
where the crowd has parked — the same feature collapses toward the fading
floor.
cards.front:
The coupled JuPedSim-to-Sionna campaign produced a result. State it, and
state exactly what it is NOT.
cards.title: The synthetic pipeline: what it shows
cards.why:
It is an INTERNAL demonstration that the differentiable-ray-tracing
pipeline emits the expected occupancy dependence, and it isolates the
signature as a property of crowd MOTION rather than static placement. It is
NOT a sim-to-real validation. The transfer claim proper is deliberately
deferred, because the decisive test needs first-party capture that does not
yet exist.

cards.back:
Acute environmental sensitivity — minor furniture or geometry shifts
invalidate trained models. Hardware and vendor heterogeneity — subcarrier
counts, proprietary phase rotations and amplitude scaling differ per
chipset. Increasing vendor restriction of raw CSI access. And fundamental
multi-person ambiguity — overlapping multipath from distinct bodies becomes
statistically entangled as occupancy grows.
cards.front:
Name the four structural limitations of CSI-only sensing the chapter
consolidates, and say what they motivate.
cards.title: The structural limits
cards.why:
Together they impose a need for frequent RE-ANCHORING to a stable reference
— which is the argument the BLE chapter then has to earn rather than
assume. The chapter is careful to say the case for that mechanism is
developed there, not presumed here.

cards.back:
(i) Periodic BLE calibration campaigns gathering ground-truth density and
flow snapshots. (ii) BLE-derived reconstruction of density scalar fields
and velocity vector fields during those campaigns. (iii) Fitting a
macroscopic crowd model — the site-specific fundamental diagram — so the
estimation target is a density field rather than a per-agent roster.
(iv) CSI-only autonomous inference between campaigns, re-anchored by the
most recent calibration rather than by contemporaneous supervision.
cards.front: Name the four tiers of the architecture, in order.
cards.title: The four tiers
cards.why:
The stratification is not organisational. Separating the calibration regime
from the inference regime is the mechanism behind the self-calibrating
claim, and it is what makes the design deployable where always-on
multi-sensor coverage cannot be assumed.

choices: It claimed a fundamental diagram; it now claims a learned closure.
It claimed a conservation-law PRIOR regularising the inference; it now supplies only the field-valued estimation TARGET.
It claimed a density field; it now claims a per-agent roster.
It was removed entirely when the physics prior was refuted.
cards.explanation:
The demotion is precise and worth stating precisely, because the two roles
sound similar and are not. A prior CONSTRAINS the solution space during
inference. A target says what quantity is being estimated. The prior was
tested and demoted; the target survived untouched, because the continuum
framing earns its place by fixing what a radio can hope to recover —
aggregate flux, not individual paths. What sustains inference between
anchoring events is the RE-ANCHORING, not a physical constraint.
cards.question:
Tier (iii) was demoted. What did it originally claim, and what does it
contribute now?
cards.title: What tier three lost

cards.back:
TOPOGRAPHIC — walls, doors, physical geometry. SENSOR — anchor positions
and sniffer coverage cells. LOGICAL — experimental zones and campaign
identifiers.
cards.front: Name the three IndoorGML layers the substrate carries and what each holds.
cards.title: Three layers, one footprint
cards.why:
The multi-layered space model lets the SAME physical footprint carry all
three without conflating semantically distinct views. The chapter argues
the set is both necessary and sufficient: omitting any one leaves either
geometry, coverage, or experimental design under-specified.

cards.back:
Primal space is a cellular partition — non-overlapping cells and their
shared boundaries, each cell a discrete sensing zone. The dual is the
Node–Relation Graph derived from that partition, encoding adjacency and
connectivity, which supplies the routing topology.
cards.front:
Explain IndoorGML's primal and dual spaces in one sentence each, and name
the dual.
cards.title: Primal and dual
cards.why:
A trap lives here. The NRG is a natural thing to reach for when asked what
drives count recoverability — and this thesis found it does NOT. Room
adjacency correlates with coverage only through the confounds it travels
with: floor area and receiver count.

cards.back:
The DENSITY AND PLACEMENT of receivers — not the room-adjacency topology of
the floor. It is fixed in the SENSOR layer.
cards.front:
What does the chapter call the single most consequential deployment
variable, and where is it fixed?
cards.title: The consequential deployment variable
cards.why:
The substrate is designed so receiver density can be specified and reasoned
about per zone rather than left implicit in the geometry. That design
choice is a direct consequence of a refuted hypothesis: the topology
fingerprint claim was tested in simulation and superseded by this one.

cards.back:
Covering a building's footfall with a chosen sensor set is monotone
submodular set-function maximisation, so a greedy placement — adding the
sensor with the largest marginal footfall coverage — carries the
Nemhauser–Wolsey–Fisher guarantee of at least 1 − 1/e of the optimum.
cards.front:
Placing a fixed budget of sniffers has a formal object. Name it, name the
guarantee, and name the trade-off it exposes.
cards.title: Placement is submodular
cards.why:
The trade-off is the real result. Covering the paths people actually take
(breadth) and concentrating sensing on the busy hub for a strong counting
signal (redundant depth) are DIFFERENT submodular objectives, so
coverage-optimal and counting-optimal placements differ and neither
dominates. That yields a Pareto front computable on a floor's footfall
surface rather than argued.

choices: It is a proof about the real building, so the deployed placement is provably near-optimal.

It is a design result on SYNTHETIC footfall — exact under standard coverage assumptions, approximate where hard line-of-sight or correlated occlusion breaks submodularity — with first-party confirmation reserved.
It does not apply, because coverage is not submodular in practice.
It applies only to the counting-optimal objective, not the coverage-optimal one.
cards.explanation:
The scoping is the defensible part. Submodularity was measured on this
problem rather than assumed — the objective came out exactly monotone
submodular with zero violations across the tested pairs — but the footfall
surface is simulated, and the assumptions that make the guarantee exact are
the ones real occlusion can break. What the framing genuinely buys is
turning a descriptive blind-spot figure into a placement objective with a
proof.
cards.question: How far does the 1 − 1/e guarantee extend in this deployment?
cards.title: The scope of the placement guarantee

cards.back:
First, heterogeneous wireless infrastructure cannot guarantee simultaneous
availability of every modality: scanners may be battery-powered, shared
with other services, or subject to regulatory duty-cycle constraints.
Second, the cost of BLE infrastructure — energy, hardware, radio-frequency
exposure — is most easily justified when operation is periodic and
purposeful.
cards.front:
Give the two practical realities that make BLE calibration a scheduled
campaign rather than a continuous stream.
cards.title: Why campaigns rather than always-on
cards.why:
The chapter's framing is worth borrowing verbatim at a defense: periodicity
is not a limitation to be overcome but the regime in which the full
cost–benefit profile of BLE sensing is optimised.

cards.back:
A physics-only model enforcing conservation exactly, forfeiting the
representational freedom needed for messy indoor propagation; a purely
data-driven model with no guarantee its density field integrates
consistently; and the intermediate — a soft, weighted residual penalty.
The intermediate is the one that was TESTED, and the verdict is negative.
cards.front:
The design chapter had to settle formally how the continuity equation
should enter inference. What spectrum did it consider, and what survives?
cards.title: Where the continuity residual was considered
cards.why:
The lasting formal point is the DESIGN PRINCIPLE, not the prior: soft,
revisable penalties are preferable to hard constraints in an inverse
problem this under-determined — together with the discipline of stating
such a component as a falsifiable hypothesis and retiring it when its
refutation condition fires.

choices: Yes — the BLE calibration handshake is verified as a timed automaton.

No, and not because verification was unavailable: the properties it would certify here are either local enough to be settled by testing, or are properties of the INSTRUMENT rather than of the sensing claim.
No — formal methods were considered out of scope from the outset.
Yes — the arming protocol's Petri net is a correctness proof for the deployment.
cards.explanation:
The option was EXAMINED rather than assumed, in two places, and declined in
both — which is a stronger position than never having looked. The arming
protocol's coloured Petri net did find real defects (a check-then-act
window between the shared process guard and the radio open, and an
interface-reset sweep bound to the wrong condition), but those are
engineering findings about a measurement instrument, not claims about
wireless sensing. And the BLE handshake has no verified model precisely
BECAUSE it has no measured deployment record to verify against —
formalising an unexercised protocol would produce confidence without
evidence.
cards.question:
Does any component of this system rest on a machine-checked correctness
argument, and why?
cards.title: The formal-verification decision

cards.back:
State the floor as a conservative place/transition net: places are cell
spaces, tokens are occupants, transitions are door crossings. Total
occupancy is then the net's P-invariant, so mass conservation holds EXACTLY
and without reference to a velocity field — the term whose unobservability
defeated the continuity prior. Decomposing a receiver's per-cell
sensitivity against that invariant yields a closed-form
count-identifiability index.
cards.front:
The second formal-methods attempt was substantive. State the formulation,
the prediction it made, and how it failed.
cards.title: The Petri net that settled its own case
cards.why:
It did not clear the pre-registered bar. The arm reading door adjacency
performed WORSE than one reading floor areas alone, and the index is
provably rank-equivalent to a single geometric scalar — so it never left
the feature class that had already failed. The formalism settled its own
case: an invariant-based index that reduces to a quantity already available
is evidence that occupancy is not recoverable from floor topology.

cards.back:
The CSI pipeline treats radio frames as opaque carriers of subcarrier data,
so 802.11n versus ac versus ax is a deployment-time configuration choice.
BLE sniffing is likewise decoupled from any specific advertising PHY or
channel map. The same geometry model, feature-extraction boundary and
inference logic would run against a different fleet unmodified.
cards.front:
The architecture claims protocol independence. State the claim, then state
exactly where it stops.
cards.title: Protocol agnosticism, and where it stops
cards.why:
It stops at the geometry and feature interfaces. The ABSOLUTE
variance-to-count mapping is device-specific, so a change of NIC calls for
a fresh calibration even when nothing else about the deployment has moved.
Claiming hardware independence without that sentence would contradict the
chapter's own strongest generalisation finding.

cards.back:
So that the eventual occupancy results INHERIT the credibility of the
design rather than borrowing it. Thresholds and analysis plans that are
frozen before capture cannot be graded post hoc.
cards.front:
Why does the chapter make the delivered-versus-pending boundary explicit
rather than presenting the delivered results alone?
cards.title: The chapter's contract
cards.why:
It is a claim about the author as much as about the work. Publishing an
empty result slot next to its frozen protocol is a commitment that can be
checked later, which is the only kind of commitment worth making.

cards.back:
Stage one — purely synthetic, coupling pedestrian simulation to ray-traced
channel synthesis, where ground truth is exact by construction. Stage two —
real measurements OTHER GROUPS collected, re-analysed under this thesis's
own reductions, which removes the simulator while keeping the labels.
Stage three — fully first-party, simultaneous CSI and device-count capture
under live occupancy.
cards.front:
Name the three methodological stages and the confound each successive stage
rules out.
cards.title: The three stages
cards.why:
Each stage inherits the validated components of the prior one, which
REDUCES but cannot eliminate the plausibility of simulation-artefact
explanations. Inherited components may still carry latent biases that only
manifest under real channels, so a stage-three discrepancy is strong but
not conclusive evidence.

cards.back:
Mean absolute error, for comparability and because a distribution's mean
must not drift unnoticed. Ranked probability score over operational bands,
measuring how much probability mass sits near the truth. Expected
calibration error, asking whether a stated confidence is HONEST. And width
at coverage, which guards the degenerate case.
cards.front:
Name the four quantities scored wherever a count is reported, and what each
guards against.
cards.title: The four metrics
cards.why:
Width at coverage is the one people forget. An interval can achieve ANY
coverage by becoming uninformative — coverage is only a virtue when the
interval still separates the bands the deployment must distinguish.

choices: MAE is not a proper scoring rule for distributions.

Scored on MAE alone the point and distributional contracts are nearly indistinguishable under environment shift; scored on band RPS and calibration error they are not remotely so — and it is the latter pair that tracks trustworthiness in a new room.
MAE is dominated by outlier windows in dense crowds.
The literature reports accuracy rather than MAE, so both are needed.
cards.explanation:
The chapter is explicit that the reason is EMPIRICAL rather than stylistic,
and the consequence is stark: a metric set reporting only MAE would have
CONCEALED the single clearest cross-environment result the thesis holds.
The first option is a true statement about scoring rules that is not the
argument made here — this is an observation about what the data did, not a
theoretical preference.
cards.question: What empirical fact justifies scoring more than mean absolute error?
cards.title: Why more than MAE

cards.back:
A pooled corpus from public multi-environment CSI benchmarks: seven
distinct indoor environments across two hardware platforms, several hundred
labelled observations.
cards.front:
Describe the tier-one corpus and say what makes its result hard to dismiss
as overfitting.
cards.title: The tier-one corpus
cards.why:
The measurements are ones this thesis DID NOT COLLECT and therefore cannot
have overfitted by instrument choice. The reductions, models and thresholds
are the thesis's own; the data is not. That separation is what makes tier
one the strongest delivered evidence in the document.

cards.back:
A no-pooling log-affine baseline is worst. A nested partial-pooling prior
improves zero-shot transfer over it. Two labelled anchors per held-out
environment improve it substantially further. An oracle with all local
labels is the floor.
cards.front:
State the leave-one-environment-out result as an ordering, and name the two
brackets.
cards.title: The calibration law
cards.why:
Quoting the ORDERING with its brackets is stronger than quoting one number.
A figure with an oracle below it and a naive baseline above it is a figure
you understand; a figure alone is one you have memorised. The mechanism is
empirical-Bayes shrinkage, and the model predicts the shape of the
recovery-versus-anchors curve rather than fitting it after the fact.

cards.back:
The counting slope is SIGN-STABLE across all seven environments while its
scale is PLATFORM-STRATIFIED. So the nested model is required rather than
optional.
cards.front:
What did fitting the partial-pooling model on the real corpus establish
about the model's STRUCTURE?
cards.title: Why the structure is required, not chosen
cards.why:
It is the empirical version of the mechanism-travels-scale-does-not claim,
and it settles a modelling question with data instead of preference. It is
also the same finding as hardware-shift-dominates, arriving from the
calibration side rather than the transfer side.

choices: Two beat the anchors and two lost; the thesis reports the mixed result.

Every one lost to two labelled anchors — because the dominant error is a session-structural offset that is not identifiable from the unlabelled target marginal, which is the ideal-joint-error term of the transfer bound.
They were inconclusive at the available sample size.
They were not run; the comparison is argued from theory.
cards.explanation:
Unsupervised optimal-transport feature alignment lost to the two-anchor
affine recalibration with a cluster-bootstrap interval entirely above zero.
Label-free manifold transport recovered only a small share of the gap. A
zero-shot conformal wrapper collapsed on exchangeability and two-anchor
anchoring repaired almost all of it. A count likelihood that wins
in-environment fails zero-shot and is rescued only by an anchored mean.
What makes this citable rather than anecdotal is that domain-adaptation
theory NAMES THE REASON IN ADVANCE: no label-free objective can remove that
offset, and a local labelled reference can.
cards.question:
Four mathematically independent LABEL-FREE alternatives were run under
pre-registered kill lines. What happened, and why?
cards.title: The four kill lines

cards.back: Feature, corpus and splits are held FIXED so that only the contract varies.
cards.front:
What single design property makes the point-versus-distributional result
hard to attack?
cards.title: The output-contract comparison design
cards.why:
Any objection of the form "your distributional model is just a better
model" is foreclosed by construction. Under shift the point contract's band
ranked-probability score degrades markedly while the distributional
contract does not move at all, and its stated confidences become MORE
honest where the point contract's become less.

cards.back:
In-environment, Mondrian split conformal gives valid intervals at usable
width — coverage on target at half-widths of a couple of people on a narrow
count range. Zero-shot cross-environment coverage COLLAPSES.
cards.front:
State what the conformal wrapper delivers in-environment, what happens
zero-shot, and why the failure is useful.
cards.title: The conformal certificate and its collapse
cards.why:
The collapse re-derives the LOCAL-ANCHOR REQUIREMENT distribution-free.
Two anchors repair almost the whole collapse. So a failure of the method
becomes independent evidence for the thesis's central architectural claim,
arriving by a route that assumes nothing about the model.

choices: That the instrument is accurate enough to count people.
That a night of uncorrected drift is NOT what limits overnight occupancy sensing — a meaningful negative finding about the recalibration interval the chapter must deliver.
That recalibration is unnecessary.
That phase features are also stable overnight.
cards.explanation:
It is a statement about the NOISE FLOOR against which occupancy claims are
read, not about accuracy. The third option overreaches badly: drift over
twelve empty hours says nothing about drift across a furniture
rearrangement or a hardware change, which are the perturbations the
recalibration policy exists for. And the fourth is contradicted by the same
section — phase-based features carry a thermal covariate, so amplitude
stability does not transfer to phase.
cards.question:
The empty-room amplitude drift floor is more than two orders of magnitude
below the perturbation a person causes. What does that settle?
cards.title: The drift floor and what it settles

cards.back:
Paced monitor-mode injection was introduced. At the higher commanded rate
the gate passes with a comfortable margin across nine simultaneous
observers, and scoping the time axis to the injector repairs its regularity
dramatically.
cards.front:
The pre-registered rate gate had never been passed. How was it passed, and
what was NOT done?
cards.title: The gate that was passed by fixing the instrument
cards.why:
What was NOT done is relax the gate. The sequence — declare a threshold,
fail it, report the failure, change the instrument, pass it — is the
strongest form this argument could take, and it is the answer to any
suggestion the gates were chosen to be passable.

cards.back:
Three zones, one per room, on the surveyed library floor. A staged
occupancy staircase per zone and band, each level in a SEATED/STILL and a
WALKING/MIXED sub-condition, with every entry and exit wall-clock stamped.
Nine analysis folds. Anchor arms comparing max-leverage selection against
random and count-extreme placement. And one induced drift event — a
controlled furniture move captured before and after.
cards.front:
Describe the frozen tier-three design: zones, staircase, sub-conditions,
folds, arms, and the one induced event.
cards.title: The campaign design
cards.why:
Day-zero empty-room blocks re-measure the tier-two bounds in the campaign's
OWN geometry, so the instrument bounds are not imported across rooms.

cards.back:
The seated/still sub-condition. It is the condition the motion-sensing
literature systematically AVOIDS, and the one the device-count channels are
expected to carry.
cards.front: Which sub-condition does the design make first-class on purpose, and why?
cards.title: The deliberately first-class condition
cards.why:
It is where the thesis's two hardest claims meet: the variance proxy
starves when nobody moves, which is exactly where Pillar 4's spectral
feature and the device-activity channel are supposed to take over.
Designing the campaign around the regime that breaks your workhorse feature
is the opposite of designing for a pass.

choices: The band advantage and the drift floor — because both depend on channel choice.

The continuity negative and the temporal/Doppler advantage — because either alone is insufficient: a prior failing only in simulation might be salvageable on hardware, and a Doppler advantage appearing only in simulation might be a ray-tracing artefact.
The anchor recovery and the conformal coverage — because both rest on the same corpus.
The census and positional legs of the BLE validation.
cards.explanation:
Recall what the three tiers are. Tier one is the re-analysis of public
corpora — delivered. Tier two is the characterisation of our own instrument
— delivered, and it bounds how every later occupancy claim must be read.
Tier three is the campaign the first two exist to make interpretable, and
it has not run: every occupancy this deployment has certified so far is
zero.

The joint demand is what makes the replication a test of the architectural
DECISION rather than of two separate findings. Joint replication would
confirm that moving from a physics prior to a temporal feature basis was
not a simulation artefact. Failure of EITHER would be a falsification event
requiring architectural revision before deployment.

Multi-day captures are required because feature distributions shift with
time-of-day occupancy and with environmental change, so one short session
cannot rule out lucky channel conditions.
cards.question:
Tier three is the pre-registered in-vivo campaign — the first-party capture
with people in the room, whose protocol is frozen and whose result slots are
labelled and empty. It demands TWO replications jointly rather than
separately. Which, and why jointly?
cards.title: The two joint replications

cards.back:
The CENSUS leg — unique advertisement counts against the scheduled,
wall-clock-stamped occupancy of the staircase. And the POSITIONAL leg —
trilateration error against a design threshold informed by reported
commodity BLE indoor resolution.
cards.front:
The campaign validates two BLE quantities. Name them and say which is
load-bearing.
cards.title: The two BLE legs
cards.why:
The census leg is load-bearing, because the calibration architecture
consumes COUNTS, not positions. The positional leg is bounded in advance by
the thesis's own Fresnel analysis: a metre-grade position may gate which
link's sensitive region a body occupies, and can never predict per-zone
phase.

cards.back:
On identical simulated frames, the calibrated pipeline must reduce density
MAE by a declared margin over the CSI-only baseline. On identical real
frames from the campaign, it must surpass the strongest published
heterogeneous-sensor packet-counting reference.
cards.front:
The calibrated-versus-baseline comparison declares two criteria that must
hold SIMULTANEOUSLY. What are they, and what supplies the plausibility?
cards.title: Two pre-registered acceptance criteria
cards.why:
The in-silico fusion study supplies an a-priori plausibility bound and NO
MORE THAN THAT: the staleness-aware modality switch reduced cross-floor
drift in simulation, which makes the criterion plausible rather than
aspirational while remaining a simulation-derived expectation until the
real frames exist.

cards.back:
The pair (T*, ε): the finite recalibration interval beyond which accuracy
degrades by more than a tolerance. The study schedules multi-day captures
across at least one furniture-rearrangement event, with ground-truth
windows from the participant instrument anchoring the drift curve, and
compares drift-triggered recalibration against fixed-interval and
no-recalibration baselines.
cards.front:
What exactly is the drift study designed to produce, and what caveat does
the thesis attach in advance?
cards.title: The RQ4 deliverable
cards.why:
The caveat is stated before the measurement: a single-testbed estimate
spanning a limited number of drift events BOUNDS, but does not by itself
ESTABLISH, generalisation across environments.

choices: Yes, entirely — all code and data are released.

Every DELIVERED result, yes: the public corpora plus the committed scripts regenerate every tier-one number without manual intervention. Re-running the tier-three pipeline additionally requires the released capture corpus, which is contingent on consent, retention and pseudonymisation obligations still open.
No — the reductions depend on infrastructure that is not public.
Only the simulation results, since the public corpora are licence-restricted.
cards.explanation:
The chapter states the current state of the three artefacts EXACTLY rather
than aspirationally, which is the whole point of a reproducibility
commitment. Capture sessions carry sidecar metadata and register against
surveyed geometry; every tier-one number regenerates from its committed
script over pinned corpora; and the first-party corpus is prepared for
release with the consent statement, retention policy and pseudonymisation
procedure recorded as OPEN OBLIGATIONS.
cards.question: Can a third party re-run the thesis's results today?
cards.title: The reproducibility commitment, stated exactly

cards.back:
DELIVERED: the cross-environment calibration law and its distribution-free
counterpart; the distributional output contract's shift robustness; and the
instrument bounds, including two results the field has not reported — the
delivered-fraction audit and the inter-receiver delivery spread.
PRE-REGISTERED BUT NOT DELIVERED: every occupancy result on first-party
hardware. The RQ4 answer is a designed measurement with a frozen protocol,
not yet a number.
cards.front:
State what the chapter can and cannot yet claim, in the order it states
them.
cards.title: The closing boundary
cards.why:
Being able to recite this boundary from memory is worth more at a defense
than any single result inside it. It is the sentence that decides whether
the committee reads the empty slots as a gap or as a discipline.

cards.back:
Periodic device-count campaigns supply labelled density observations that
anchor CSI inference. CSI runs autonomously between campaigns under the
resulting calibration. And a shared crowd model reconciles the two
modalities over time.
cards.front: Name the three roles the self-calibrating architecture rests on.
cards.title: The three interlocking roles
cards.why:
The middle role is the deployment claim. Anything can be accurate while
supervised; the architecture's value is what happens in the interval when
nothing is supervising it.

cards.back:
Through a carry-rate correction: the fraction of occupants bearing a
detectable device is estimated from co-located ground-truth headcounts
collected during short calibration windows.
cards.front:
How do raw device counts become occupant-density labels, and what happens
to the uncertainty in that conversion?
cards.title: The label-noise path
cards.why:
The residual uncertainty of that estimate propagates as a LABEL-NOISE term
into the CSI training objective. It is not discarded and it is not silently
absorbed into the point estimate — which is the same propagate-rather-than-
correct discipline the output contract imposes everywhere else.

choices: That BLE should be weighted more heavily at all densities.
That a naive CONSTANT blend is dominated: the device count wins while fresh, CSI wins once the anchor is stale, so the correct estimator is a confidence-weighted switch on anchor staleness.
That CSI should be discarded whenever an anchor is available.
That the two modalities should be averaged with weights fitted per environment.
cards.explanation:
Dominated is the operative word: the switch tracks the LOWER ENVELOPE of
the two modalities across the full range of advertising cadence, so no
fixed blend can match it. The study also changed how BLE was modelled — as
an INDEPENDENT device counter, a bias-correctable occupancy reference,
rather than a signal regressed against ground truth. That modelling choice
is what makes the result about complementarity in TIME rather than about a
better regression.
cards.question:
The first coupled-simulation study yielded a sharper claim than the
original "reconcile by a shared model". What was it?
cards.title: The switch, not the blend

cards.back:
A recursive Bayesian (Kalman) filter over a latent state comprising the
crowd count and the slowly-drifting per-environment calibration. The device
count is a rare, low-variance measurement; CSI a frequent, higher-variance
one whose calibration drifts.
cards.front:
State Pillar 3: what single object are the fusion switch and the drift
trigger two readouts of?
cards.title: The unification
cards.why:
Fusion is the filter's GAIN — immediately after an anchor its posterior
variance is low and it dominates, and as time passes the filter leans on
CSI, so the exponential staleness weight IS the gain trajectory. The
trigger is a sequential change-point stopping rule on the filter's
innovation, with a single cost knob in place of a calendar.

cards.back:
It DEMOTED the pilot's headline figures, and they are reported demoted. The
cross-modal disagreement tracks true count error with a substantially
weaker correlation and a wide interval at the seed-cluster unit, and the
change-point rule FAILS an accuracy-equivalence test against the fixed
schedule while spending roughly half its calibration budget.
cards.front:
What did the powered replication do to Pillar 3's numbers, and how is the
claim now stated?
cards.title: The demotion, stated first
cards.why:
So the demonstrated payoff is the COST FRONTIER, not accuracy parity.
Offering that sentence unprompted is the difference between a demotion that
reads as rigour and one that reads as a correction extracted under
questioning.

cards.back:
It was tested across three independent in-silico testbeds with
pre-registered margins, and the second time the confidence intervals fell
entirely inside the refutation region AND were invariant to the velocity
closure.
cards.front:
The continuity prior is refuted a second time in this chapter. What is
different about this refutation?
cards.title: The second refutation
cards.why:
Closure-invariance is the decisive property. A conservation term whose
benefit is unchanged when the conservation law is replaced by its opposite
is not functioning as a physical constraint. The architecture accordingly
retains generic regularisation of the ill-posed inverse and drops the
physics prior; the load-bearing temporal mechanism is the state-space
filter.

cards.back:
Because the prior is attractive enough that it WILL be proposed again, and
the evidence that retires it is exactly reproducible.
cards.front:
Why does the chapter keep the refutation on the record rather than simply
removing the component?
cards.title: Why keep the negative in the design chapter
cards.why:
A negative that cannot be reproduced forecloses nothing — it is just an
anecdote about one team's failure. Reproducibility is what converts a
disappointment into a contribution.

choices: That the trigger implementation has a bug in its false-alarm calibration.
That a purely statistical self-trigger is exquisitely sensitive to physically meaningless micro-drift and cannot ALONE decide when a recalibration campaign is worth its cost.
That the room was not actually empty.
That twelve hours is too short a baseline to calibrate a trigger.
cards.explanation:
The first option is ruled out by the measurement itself: the pre-registered
per-window false-alarm calibration HOLDS, with the realised rate sitting
inside its expected interval. The trigger is behaving exactly as designed
and firing anyway, on a detected shift of a few thousandths of a decibel —
a fraction of the empty-room noise. That is the point. Statistical
significance is not physical significance, and a trigger that cannot tell
them apart will spend a calibration budget on nothing.
cards.question:
On twelve certified-empty hours, the anytime-valid statistical trigger
fired on a third of the streams. What does that establish?
cards.title: The measured constraint on triggering

cards.back:
First, the deployed trigger tests DISAGREEMENT AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT
DEVICE-COUNT REFERENCE, not the CSI stream against its own history. Second,
it carries a pre-registered MAGNITUDE GATE stating what shift is worth a
campaign, on top of the statistical gate.
cards.front:
Two design rules follow from the certified-empty false-trigger result. Name
both.
cards.title: The two design rules that follow
cards.why:
Both are carried into the evaluation protocol, which is what makes them
design rules rather than lessons. The referenced trigger is also the reason
the device-activity channel is architecturally load-bearing rather than a
curiosity: a self-referential trigger has nothing to disagree with.

cards.back:
A hysteresis condition: the exceedance must persist across at least two
consecutive campaigns before a recalibration is issued.
cards.front: Besides the magnitude gate, what bounds the false-trigger rate?
cards.title: Hysteresis
cards.why:
It converts an instantaneous excursion into a sustained one, which is the
cheapest available defence against the exact failure the certified-empty
measurement exposed — a single window of meaningless micro-drift crossing a
threshold.

cards.back:
A drift metric — the rolling divergence between the device-anchored density
and the CSI-predicted density — is monitored continuously against a
threshold derived from the reference's own noise. Crossing it, with
hysteresis and a magnitude gate, demands a campaign. The campaign
re-anchors the model, and autonomous inference resumes.
cards.front:
Summarise the calibration–inference–drift loop in the language of a
controller.
cards.title: The loop, stated as a controller
cards.why:
The one-line summary the chapter itself offers is worth memorising:
recalibration is demanded by EVIDENCE rather than by elapsed time. That
sentence is the whole difference between a schedule and a policy.

choices: Measured on the deployed fleet across multiple weeks.
In-silico, and labelled as such, with the powered replication's demotions applied — real multi-week drift is the leg that would settle it.
Validated on public corpora under the thesis's own reductions.
Derived analytically, so no empirical standing is claimed.
cards.explanation:
The third option is true of the CALIBRATION results in the evaluation
chapter, not of fusion — mixing them up is the easiest way to overclaim
here. This chapter's mechanism is developed analytically AND exercised in
simulation, with one measured first-party constraint from the
certified-empty hours. That constraint is real and it is a NEGATIVE. The
positive fusion results remain in-silico.
cards.question:
What is the evidential standing of this chapter's fusion and trigger
results?
cards.title: What is in-silico and what is not

cards.back:
A university library on the evening before examinations, a transit
concourse at rush hour, and an open-plan office during an unannounced fire
drill.
cards.front:
The chapter opens with three scenes. Name them, and say what they have in
common.
cards.title: The opening image
cards.why:
In each, one quantity — how many people are present, and where — silently
governs decisions from the mundane to the life-critical. The scenes span
the three application domains the chapter then argues for: safety, energy
management and space utilisation.

choices: No prior solutions exist for indoor crowd counting.
Prior solutions exist in three families, and each exacts a price in privacy, cost, coverage, or occupant cooperation.
The wireless hardware needed has only recently become affordable.
Regulators have not agreed on an occupancy standard.
cards.explanation:
The chapter is explicit that the answer lies NOT in any absence of prior
solutions but in the recurring shortcomings of each. Vision gives high
spatial resolution and raises acute privacy concerns while collapsing under
occlusion and poor light. Infrared and thermal sidestep identity disclosure
but stay expensive at scale and give only zone-level occupancy.
Device-based methods shed the line-of-sight requirement but depend on user
cooperation and near-universal device carriage, systematically
undercounting populations with low adoption or powered-off radios.
cards.question: The introduction argues the problem remains open. What is its reason?
cards.title: Why the problem stays open

cards.back:
CSI exposes per-subcarrier amplitude and phase across every antenna pair in
an OFDM system, and RSSI averages exactly that structure away. Bodies
scatter, absorb and reflect propagating wavefronts, perturbing the complex
channel coefficients in ways that accumulate across subcarriers as
occupancy grows.
cards.front:
Give the one-sentence physical case for CSI over RSSI, then the one-sentence
case for why bodies show up in it at all.
cards.title: The case for CSI over RSSI
cards.why:
Both halves are needed. The first says the observable is rich; the second
says the richness is coupled to the thing you want to measure. Neither
alone makes a sensing case.

cards.back:
Site specificity — a model trained in one room degrades in a geometrically
different one. Limited spatial coverage — single link-pairs struggle on
large or irregular floors, and aggregating links costs combinatorial
calibration. Poor performance at occupancy extremes — accuracy plateaus
beyond a handful of occupants and is unreliable at one or two. Baseline
drift — firmware and hardware changes shift phase and amplitude over weeks
without warning.
cards.front:
Name the four gaps the introduction says have blocked real-world deployment
of CSI crowd counting.
cards.title: The four documented gaps
cards.why:
The chapter's closing claim is about the CONJUNCTION: no published system
simultaneously achieves cross-site generalisability, scalable deployment
and sustained accuracy without manual recalibration. Any one of the four
has been addressed somewhere.

cards.back:
First, reimagine a moving crowd not as a set of individuals to be tracked
but as a continuum whose state is an aggregate density field, so the
estimation target becomes a field rather than a tangle of trajectories.
Second, treat periodic BLE calibration campaigns as a recurring source of
ground truth that re-anchors a drifting CSI sensor, without ever demanding
continuous device carriage.
cards.front:
State the thesis's central proposition as the introduction frames it — two
ideas from different traditions.
cards.title: The central proposition
cards.why:
The second idea contains its own defence. BLE here is a CONTROLLED-CAMPAIGN
instrument in which known occupancy states are established under
coordinated conditions — not a passive always-on occupancy monitor, which
is the role the literature has already shown device-carriage assumptions
undermine.

choices: Because BLE radios consume too much power to run continuously.
Because a campaign establishes KNOWN occupancy states under coordinated conditions, decoupling the calibration loop from unreliable spontaneous device presence.
Because BLE scanning at all times would breach the data-protection assessment.
Because passive BLE cannot detect randomised addresses.
cards.explanation:
The self-calibration loop fires from snapshot EVENTS, which decouples
recalibration from the passive-coverage weakness prior literature
criticises. The other options are all true-ish statements about BLE that
are not the reason given: duty-cycle and power do appear later as
practical arguments for periodicity, and randomisation is discussed as the
privacy floor under device counting, but neither is what makes the campaign
framing load-bearing here.
cards.question:
Why does the introduction insist BLE is used as a campaign instrument
rather than as an always-on monitor?
cards.title: What "campaign" buys

cards.back:
An earlier version made the continuity equation a HARD PHYSICS PRIOR
bounding the solution space. That prior does not, on indoor geometry,
outperform generic smoothing. What remains load-bearing is not a physical
prior but two commitments: the BLE-anchored calibration loop, and
deliberate attention to WHICH features and WHICH kind of domain shift
govern whether a trained counter survives a move.
cards.front:
The introduction retracts part of its own earlier proposal. What, and what
replaces it?
cards.title: The retraction, stated up front
cards.why:
Placing the retraction in chapter one is a rhetorical decision with a
defensive purpose. A committee that discovers a refutation in chapter seven
suspects it was discovered late. Announcing it in the first pages says the
document was rebuilt around it.

cards.back:
Autonomy: between calibration campaigns the system should sustain accurate
inference on its own and degrade GRACEFULLY — predictably rather than
catastrophically — as the environment drifts, recalibrating only when
accumulated drift warrants it.
cards.front:
The chapter names the architecture's "defining ambition". What is it, and
what does the qualifier mean?
cards.title: Graceful degradation
cards.why:
"Predictably rather than catastrophically" is the operative clause and it
is what the output contract later makes measurable. A system whose error
grows in a known way is deployable; one that fails silently is not, however
good its average.

choices: Yes — an aggregate count discloses nothing identifiable, so the modality is private by construction.

It is privacy-preserving in what it RELEASES, but the channel it reads can be observed passively, through walls, and without the awareness of those counted — so privacy is engineered and audited, not granted.
No — CSI is strictly more invasive than a camera because it works through walls.
The question is out of scope; privacy is handled by the ethics appendix.
cards.explanation:
The chapter states this caveat explicitly and honours it throughout. The
first option is the trap and it is the answer most people give — it is half
right, which is why it is dangerous. The distinction that matters is
between what a system OUTPUTS and what a system CAN OBSERVE. The consequence
is a concrete posture: consent, data-handling and identifier-randomisation
commitments in the supporting appendix, rather than a claim that the
modality is inherently safe.
cards.question:
A committee member says: "So your system is privacy-preserving by design,
unlike a camera." How does the introduction's own position answer that?
cards.title: The privacy caveat

cards.back:
So that every question receives ORIGINAL EMPIRICAL treatment rather than a
survey of prior work. Each answering chapter delivers purpose-designed
experiments, re-analyses of public corpora under the thesis's own
reductions, or pre-registered protocols with measured instrument bounds.
None functions as a literature synthesis.
cards.front:
Why does the thesis map each research question onto its own experimental
chapter, and what does the mapping guarantee?
cards.title: One question, one chapter
cards.why:
The architectural point: the cumulative argument gets assembled incrementally
from independently verifiable blocks rather than asserted in the abstract.
It is also what makes it possible to record where a component hypothesis did
not survive, without the whole argument collapsing.

cards.back:
An occupancy sensor that rides on the WiFi and BLE infrastructure already
present in nearly every modern building, and that calibrates itself on a
schedule rather than under an engineer's supervision.
cards.front:
State the concrete long-term ambition that frames the four research
questions.
cards.title: The long-term ambition
cards.why:
The second clause is the thesis. Riding on existing infrastructure is a
deployment argument many papers make; calibrating without an engineer is
the one that requires a reference channel, a drift metric and a policy —
which is exactly what objectives O1 and RQ4 are for.

cards.back:
Microscopic — individual pedestrians as discrete entities, governed by
force-based rules or stochastic lattice transitions. Mesoscopic — the
statistical distribution of agents over velocity or heading states, without
resolving every trajectory. Macroscopic — the crowd as a compressible
continuum with a density field and a mean velocity field, individual
identities abstracted away.
cards.front: Name the three tiers of pedestrian-crowd models and what each represents.
cards.title: The three tiers
cards.why:
The thesis chooses macroscopic for a stated reason: RF channel
perturbations aggregate over the spatial extent of a link and are therefore
