more naturally matched to continuum density fields than to per-agent state
vectors.

choices: Yes — RF cannot resolve individuals in a crowd.
No — device-free RF tracking of individuals has been demonstrated elsewhere; the choice reflects the low spatial resolution of the links employed HERE.
Yes, above about four occupants, where multipath becomes entangled.
The chapter does not address it.
cards.explanation:
The distinction matters because overclaiming here is easy and would be
caught. The macroscopic tier is a PRACTICALLY MOTIVATED design choice for
this deployment's link geometry, not a physical impossibility result. A
committee member who has read the device-free tracking literature will know
the difference, and conceding it costs nothing while defending it costs the
chapter's credibility.
cards.question: Is the macroscopic choice a claim that per-agent RF tracking is impossible?
cards.title: The honest qualifier on that choice

cards.back:
Because it is not postulated independently — it EMERGES from the
aggregation of microscopic rules. The social-force model's continuous
interactions spontaneously generate lane formation, arching and clogging at
bottlenecks, and stop-and-go waves; individual behavioural noise tends to
average out at the collective scale.
cards.front: Why is the continuum description trustworthy rather than merely convenient?
cards.title: What licenses the continuum
cards.why:
Their ensemble averages over many agents yield smooth, slowly varying
density and flux fields, and that smoothness is exactly what licenses the
macroscopic law. The argument runs bottom-up, which is why the chapter
spends a section on microscopic foundations it does not otherwise need.

cards.back:
Social force — each pedestrian obeys a Newtonian equation of motion with a
driving term relaxing velocity toward a desired heading, plus pairwise
repulsive social forces and boundary forces. Floor-field cellular automata
— space is a lattice and forces are replaced by a stochastic transition
rule weighted by a static field encoding distance to exits and a dynamic
field encoding the trace left by preceding movers.
cards.front:
Name the two microscopic paradigms and the essential difference between
them.
cards.title: The two microscopic paradigms
cards.why:
Forces versus probabilities, continuous versus discretised space. They are
interchangeable microscopic engines, and the lattice discretisation trades
spatial resolution against speed — which is the practical reason a
simulator picks one.

cards.back:
Density changes at any point are driven SOLELY by net flux divergence, with
no source or sink terms. It follows from mass conservation under the
HOMOGENEOUS-VELOCITY assumption: all pedestrians within an infinitesimal
volume share a common mean velocity.
cards.front:
State the continuity equation in words, name the assumption that produces
it, and say what it is exactly.
cards.title: The conservation law and its assumption
cards.why:
It is precisely the first-order Lighthill–Whitham–Richards scalar
conservation law. As a kinematic identity the conservation law is EXACT;
what is an approximation is the homogeneous-velocity closure, and the
chapter flags that assumption as load-bearing rather than burying it.

cards.back:
It contains TWO unknown fields — density and velocity — so it is
underdetermined. The fundamental diagram resolves this by expressing speed
as a single-valued function of density.
cards.front: Why can the continuity equation not be integrated on its own?
cards.title: Why a closure is mandatory
cards.why:
This is why "we use the continuity equation" is never a complete statement
of a model. The conservation law is the portable part; the closure is the
part that encodes local pedestrian culture, corridor surface and typical
flow regime, and it is what a site campaign re-fits.

choices: Only the scalar speed–density closure f(ρ); the conservation law carries no geometric assumptions.
The closure f(ρ) — but ALSO the eikonal direction field, obstacle geometry, corridor widths and exit boundary conditions, which must be re-specified separately.
The whole model, since multipath is site-specific.
Nothing — the continuum model is geometry-independent by construction.
cards.explanation:
The first option is the seductive half-truth and it is exactly what an
earlier draft of this section said. The conservation structure IS portable
and carries no assumptions about corridor widths or exit configurations —
that part is right. But the chapter adds an important qualification: only
the SCALAR CLOSURE is treated as a portable, site-calibratable parameter,
not the broader spatial formulation. Claiming that a short calibration
campaign adapts the whole model to a new geometry would overstate what the
campaign buys.
cards.question: Moving the model to a new building, what must be refitted?
cards.title: What actually has to be refitted

cards.back:
A conventional supervised data loss is augmented with a PHYSICS-RESIDUAL
loss penalising violation of the governing partial differential equation at
collocation points. For crowd density the residual is the continuity
equation closed by a fundamental diagram, so the network is rewarded for
predictions that conserve mass and respect the empirical speed–density
relation.
cards.front:
How does a physics-informed network embed a conservation law, and why did
this thesis expect it to help?
cards.title: The physics-informed construction
cards.why:
The expectation was reasonable. In traffic-state estimation the same
construction demonstrably reduces error, and where labelled density
observations are scarce — as they are for RF sensing — the physics term
should carry disproportionate weight.

choices: It compared the prior against a stronger baseline on more data.

It swapped the CLOSURE — a physically correct one, a constant one, and an ANTI-PHYSICAL increasing one — and found identical high-density error, while a plain smoothing prior with no conservation content beat all three.
It removed the physics term entirely and measured the difference.
It ran the comparison across three independent testbeds.
cards.explanation:
The mismatch is the whole argument. Removing a term and finding no
difference proves only that the term was inert. Replacing the physics with
its OPPOSITE and finding no difference proves the term was never acting as
physics in the first place — it was doing generic smoothing, and doing it
worse than a smoother designed for the job. The third option is the
ordinary ablation and the fourth is a robustness measure; both were also
done, and neither is what makes the negative decisive.
cards.question:
What is the decisive design feature of the ablation that refuted the
continuity prior?
cards.title: The ablation that settled it

cards.back:
That literature reports the physics term's contribution is
regime-dependent: its optimal weight shrinks as data grow, a LEARNED
fundamental diagram outperforms a fixed parametric one, and the gains
concentrate in the strong-directed-flow, data-sparse regime.
cards.front:
The refutation is presented as CONSISTENT with the physics-informed
literature rather than contradicting it. How?
cards.title: Consistent with, not contrary to
cards.why:
None of which describes the low-directed-flow indoor geometries tested
here. Framing a negative as a regime boundary rather than a contradiction
is both more accurate and much harder to attack — it predicts where the
prior WOULD work, and the chapter accordingly leaves one narrow test open
for sustained uni-directional bottleneck flow.

cards.back:
On IDENTICAL data, a quasi-static amplitude statistic carries almost no
count information and adding receivers does not help, whereas a
Doppler-aware temporal feature lifts the CSI-to-count fit several-fold.
cards.front:
The experiment that sank the fluid prior also pointed to its replacement.
What did it show?
cards.title: What replaced it
cards.why:
The recoverable count lives in the TEMPORAL, VELOCITY-DEPENDENT
fine-structure of the channel, not in its static amplitude. That relocation
is the chapter's defensible inference contribution, and it is mirrored on
real stationary crowds by a velocity-aware bandwidth feature in the
literature. All the chapter's own figures here are in-silico and await
real-channel confirmation.

cards.back:
Whether the SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION of density — rather than its integral — is
recoverable from a finite set of aggregate RF link observations.
cards.front: The chapter names its own primary unproven contribution. What is it?
cards.title: The unproven premise, named
cards.why:
Two established pillars support the premise separately: device-free CSI
recovers aggregate counts from a crowd's bulk dielectric loading, and
continuum models parameterise the same density field. What neither
establishes JOINTLY is the spatial recovery, and the chapter says so rather
than letting the two citations imply it.

cards.back:
A microscopic pedestrian simulator propagates agents through floor-plan
geometry, producing per-frame trajectories. A trajectory analytics layer
bins those positions into time-resolved density maps that serve as
ground-truth labels. A differentiable ray tracer renders per-link complex
channel coefficients from the same scene, yielding paired CSI-and-density
samples.
cards.front:
Name the three stages of the coupled simulation pipeline and what each
produces.
cards.title: The coupled pipeline
cards.why:
Physical consistency is guaranteed BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the point: it
is the only way to get paired data at the scale and label accuracy the
ablations needed. It is also why the chapter's results are labelled
in-silico rather than validated.

cards.back:
Because the same controlled setting produced BOTH findings: the ablation
that retired the physics prior, and the feature comparison that located the
count in the temporal structure. A testbed that can only confirm is not a
testbed.
cards.front:
Why does the chapter argue the coupled pipeline earned its keep even though
its headline result was a refutation?
cards.title: The value of a negative testbed
cards.why:
It is also the argument for the pipeline's continued existence. The
synthetic-transfer hypothesis is deferred rather than abandoned — the
pipeline is built and exercised, and it reactivates the moment a real
target set with occupants exists.

cards.back:
Because of the nature of the work. CSI sensing is exquisitely sensitive to
deployment context and it is HARDWARE-GATED: claims about calibration
stability, geometry-faithful simulation, or which features survive an
environment change can only be adjudicated as the corresponding capture
sets and analysis tools come online.
cards.front:
Why does the thesis commit to living hypotheses rather than deferring its
verdict to a concluding chapter?
cards.title: Why living hypotheses
cards.why:
Writing the hypotheses down before the data arrive keeps the record honest.
A thesis that states its claims after seeing its results cannot demonstrate
it did not fit them to what it found.

cards.back:
Lifecycle state — candidate, chosen, deferred, refuted, superseded — which
tracks the DECISION history. Evidence strength — speculative, plausible,
supported, strong — which tracks what the claim has EARNED.
cards.front:
Name the two axes every hypothesis note carries and give the values of
each.
cards.title: The two axes
cards.why:
They are deliberately orthogonal, and the orthogonality is the point: a
claim can be firmly chosen yet only plausible, and one central to an early
draft can be honestly retired once its refutation condition fires.
Collapsing them into a single confidence number is how a portfolio starts
lying about itself.

choices: It was cross-environment generalisation; it is now a simulation-to-real physics bridge, after the fluid prior was confirmed.
It was a simulation-to-real physics bridge resting on a fluid-dynamics prior; the prior was tested and refuted, so O3 was rebuilt around the determinants of cross-deployment generalisation.
It was merged into O2 once the forward physics was settled.
It was narrowed to synthetic pretraining only, since the hardware leg is deferred.
cards.explanation:
The original framing did not survive contact with the evidence: the fluid
prior was refuted, and the synthetic-transfer leg awaits first-party
hardware. Rebuilding O3 around what the data DO support — which shift
dominates, which features survive, where the robust count signal lives —
turns it into the best-evidenced objective in the chapter. That is worth
saying plainly at a defense: the objective was not weakened by the
refutation, it was strengthened.
cards.question: Objective O3 was reformulated. What was it, what is it now, and why?
cards.title: O3, rebuilt

cards.back:
The output of a CSI occupancy estimator is a predictive distribution over
counts, P(N = k), with operational bands obtained by marginalisation at
query time — and this contract is shift-robust in a way the point contract
is not.
cards.front:
State the distributional output contract and the two measured facts that
forced it.
cards.title: The output contract
cards.why:
Fact one: the count mapping does not transfer cold across environments, so
a real leave-one-environment-out error against a predict-the-mean baseline
is a thin margin for a headline estimand. Fact two: the question a building
actually asks is almost never "how many" but "which band, and how sure".

cards.back:
On the pooled cross-environment corpus, holding the feature, the corpus and
the splits fixed so that ONLY THE CONTRACT VARIES.
cards.front:
How was the point-versus-distributional comparison run so that the
comparison is about the CONTRACT and nothing else?
cards.title: How the contract was tested
cards.why:
That design is what makes the result citable. Under shift the point
estimator's band ranked-probability score degrades by 27 per cent while the
discrete distribution does not move at all, and its stated confidences stay
honest where the point estimator's do not. Same features, same data, same
splits — so the difference cannot be attributed to a better model.

cards.back:
A little point accuracy in the EASY regime — in-environment error is
slightly worse than the point model's — and almost nothing in the hard one.
cards.front: The distributional contract is not free. What does it cost, and where?
cards.title: What the contract costs
cards.why:
Saying so is a strength rather than a concession. It shows the comparison
was scored honestly on the metric that favours the incumbent, and it
locates the trade precisely: you pay in the regime where you did not need
the help.

choices: Per-environment prediction intervals with guaranteed nominal coverage under drift.

A mechanism result plus a finite-sample limitation: in-environment validity at usable width, zero-shot collapse where exchangeability fails, and near-complete repair from two anchors — but per-environment validity is NOT uniform at commodity calibration sizes.
Nothing — the conformal layer was abandoned when zero-shot coverage collapsed.
Guaranteed coverage, provided the calibration set exceeds a computable minimum size.
cards.explanation:
The evidence is mixed in an informative way and the claim is scoped to it.
The zero-shot collapse is not a failure of the method; it is the
exchangeability assumption failing, and the fact that two anchors almost
completely repair it RE-DERIVES the local-anchor requirement by a
distribution-free route. The fourth option is the seductive one, and the
chapter forecloses it: exact conditional coverage is PROVABLY unattainable
at finite sample, which bounds what any per-environment claim may promise.
cards.question: What exactly does the thesis claim for conformal coverage?
cards.title: The conformal claim, scoped

cards.back:
The O1 hypotheses — reference sufficiency, periodic recalibration, drift
triggering, plus the device–person pair that defends their shared premise.
Shared logic: CSI counts drift as an environment changes, so the system
needs an independent, self-labelling reference that can re-anchor it, and
it needs to know when to spend that reference.
cards.front:
What is the calibration spine, what logic do its hypotheses share, and what
cannot settle it?
cards.title: The calibration spine
cards.why:
Simulation cannot settle it. The decisive test is a multi-week, multi-site
hardware capture with a measured drift curve, which the evaluation chapter
reserves. That is why the spine sits at plausible while the O3 material
sits at supported.

cards.back:
That the anchor counts RADIOS while the thesis claims to count PEOPLE. Not
everyone carries an advertising device, some carry several, and address
randomisation inflates the identifier tally above the device tally.
cards.front:
The chapter calls one joint the "weakest joint in the calibration spine".
Which, and what is the standard remedy it rejects?
cards.title: The devices-versus-people problem
cards.why:
The standard remedy is to multiply by a conversion factor measured in
somebody else's building and hope it holds. Two objections: the factor is
not stationary — it varies by hour, by day, and more sharply across crowd
TYPES — and a point correction converts an unknown bias into a confident
number, moving the estimate without widening it, which is precisely the
wrong response to not knowing something.

cards.back:
It operates two counters that fail DIFFERENTLY. CSI perturbation responds
to bodies, device-free, indifferent to what those bodies carry. Device
activity responds to radios and is indifferent to whether they move. Two
observations of one occupancy state with disjoint nuisance structures
determine both the count and the ratio, where either alone leaves them
confounded.
cards.front:
How does the thesis propose to do better than an imported conversion
factor, and what is the identification argument?
cards.title: Joint identification
cards.why:
And the residual uncertainty is PROPAGATED, not corrected — it widens the
predictive distribution rather than displacing a point estimate, so a count
that is uncertain because the crowd is unusual is reported as uncertain.

choices: The two channels share a clock, so their errors are correlated by construction.

Identifiability is ARGUED, not demonstrated — two noisy channels identify a ratio only if their nuisance structures are genuinely disjoint and the occupancy range is wide enough to separate their response curves.
The CSI channel cannot observe device carriage at all, so the ratio is unidentifiable in principle.
The participant instrument makes the ratio measured, so no caveat remains.
cards.explanation:
And the chapter goes further, predicting WHERE it will be uneven: the CSI
leg is concave and saturating, so the joint fit should be strongest in the
middle of the density range and weakest at both ends — exactly where the
device leg is most reliable. That is the complementarity the chapter argues
for, and also a reason to expect identification to be uneven rather than
uniform. Predicting the shape of your own weakness before measuring it is a
strong defensive position.
cards.question:
The thesis is careful about what joint identification does NOT yet deliver.
What is the caveat?
cards.title: The honest limit of the identification argument

cards.back:
That injecting the one-dimensional mass-conservation continuity equation,
closed by a fundamental diagram, as a physics-informed regulariser would
lower CSI density-estimation error in the high-density regime. A
mismatched-closure ablation showed the apparent gain was INDEPENDENT of the
velocity closure — physically correct, constant and anti-physical closures
gave identical high-density error — and a plain smoothness prior with no
conservation content outperformed all of them.
cards.front:
State the refuted hypothesis, the ablation that killed it, and why it is
kept on the record.
cards.title: The refuted hypothesis
cards.why:
Kept on the record because the prior is attractive enough that it will be
proposed again, and the evidence that retires it is exactly reproducible.
A negative that is not reproducible cannot foreclose anything.

cards.back:
**Refuted** means the claim was wrong and the question it asked is closed.
The continuity prior is refuted: mass conservation as a training penalty
does not beat plain smoothing indoors, and nobody should try it again on
this kind of geometry.

**Superseded** means the claim was wrong about the VARIABLE, but the
question survived and got a better answer. The original claim was that a
floor's room-adjacency topology predicts how well you can count on it. It
does not — topology only correlates with coverage through the things it
travels with, floor area and how many receivers you placed. Hold those
fixed and the signal vanishes. What actually drives recoverability is
receiver DENSITY and placement, and that is now its own hypothesis.
cards.front:
Your hypothesis table has one row marked "superseded" and another marked
"refuted". A committee member asks what the difference is, and why it
matters to them.
cards.title: Superseded is not refuted
cards.why:
Why it matters to a committee: the two labels imply different things about
what is left to do. A refuted claim leaves a hole in the argument that
something else must fill. A superseded one leaves a successor already
carrying the weight.

Being able to say which is which is the difference between "we were wrong"
and "we were wrong about the variable, and here is the right one".

cards.back:
The literal identity "occupancy EQUALS the number of detached eigenvalue
modes". It is retired because occupancy is a coherent low-rank perturbation
rather than N independent spikes — the mode count ranges over dozens for
occupancies of only a handful.
cards.front:
Part of the spectral hypothesis has already fired its own refutation
condition. Which part, and why did it fail?
cards.title: The retired half of Pillar 2a
cards.why:
What survives is the STRUCTURAL form: mode count tracks occupancy
monotonically and concavely, and the aspect-ratio scaling of the detection
budget holds strictly. On amplitude-only data the spectral feature is
furthermore variance-equivalent, so complex-CSI replication is the
remaining leg. Being able to say which half died is worth more than
defending the whole.

cards.back:
The hypotheses are the EMPIRICAL contract — measurable claims with
refutation conditions. Taken singly they are a set of measurements. The
pillars state the THEORETICAL contribution those measurements instantiate:
four formal models, each grounded in a result already in hand, each
unifying several hypotheses, each predicting something testable.
cards.front:
What do the four pillars add that the hypotheses do not, and what is their
one-sentence through-line?
cards.title: The four pillars, and why they exist
cards.why:
The through-line: a single scattering-derived link, reparameterised per
environment by a hierarchical calibration model, tracked over time by a
state-space filter, with the two hard cases — still crowds and sensor
placement — handled by spectral and submodular arguments.

cards.back:
A packet-rate gate. Two hypotheses — the temporal/Doppler count locus and
any drift claim resting on fine time structure — presumed a rate the
instrument had not demonstrated, and applied verbatim the pre-registered
rate gate admitted none of the captures held at that time.
cards.front:
Besides the missing occupancy capture, the chapter names a second gap. What
was it, and what happened to it?
cards.title: The second, newer gap
cards.why:
The gate was NOT relaxed; the instrument was fixed. Paced monitor-mode
injection now passes the delivered-rate gate with margin across nine
simultaneous observers. That sequence — declare the gate, fail it, report
the failure, then pass it by changing the instrument — is the strongest
form the argument could take.

cards.back:
Ten Raspberry Pi 5 nodes, each with an Intel AX210 on PCIe running in
monitor mode as its CSI radio, with the Pi's own wireless interface
reserved for management. Nine observe; one is the paced illuminator.
cards.front: Describe the fleet in one sentence, and say what Ansible owns.
cards.title: The fleet
cards.why:
Ansible owns NODE IDENTITY end to end: the inventory hostname is
simultaneously the system hostname, the tailnet name, the S3 prefix and the
telemetry host name — so a record traces to the machine that produced it
without a lookup table.

choices: There is no ESP32 sidecar tier; and the fleet is hardware-complete but not evidentially complete, because the participant instrument has never run a session.
There is no BLE controller; and the fleet has only six nodes.
The AX210s cannot do monitor mode; and the illuminator is an access point.
There is no PostGIS substrate; and node identity is managed by hand.
cards.explanation:
An earlier design provisioned ESP32 modules as WiFi-6 stimulus and
auxiliary capture at a complementary vantage; the deployment did not take
it up, and spatial diversity comes from the ten-node array instead. The
second correction is the sharper one: multi-node coordinated capture is NO
LONGER pending — six nodes ran twelve continuous hours and produced
millions of records — but the participant instrument, though built and
deployed, has never run a session. That absence, not any missing hardware,
is what keeps the experimental programme short of proven.
cards.question: The chapter owes two corrections about the fleet. Which pair is right?
cards.title: Two corrections to the fleet description

cards.back:
Genuine 2x2 HE20 records at 242 tones, and at 160 MHz monitor width
996-tone HE80 records, with hardware timestamps resolving to a few
nanoseconds. That is an order of magnitude beyond the 56 occupied
subcarriers of the 802.11n legacy floor.
cards.front:
What does the AX210 capture path actually deliver, and how does it compare
to the platform most CSI papers were written on?
cards.title: What the adapter yields
cards.why:
It matters for the spectral pillar specifically: p is antennas times
subcarriers, so a richer tone grid moves the aspect ratio and therefore the
detection budget. It also matters for comparability — results on 56
subcarriers are not automatically results on 996.

cards.back:
Delivery, resolved against the transmitter's OWN counter rather than
estimated. Amplitude drift, an empty-room two-chain CSI ratio holding to a
few thousandths of a decibel and independently reproduced by a second
pipeline. Phase drift, which unlike amplitude drift is THERMAL — per-node
slope rank-ordered with mean SoC temperature. And timing, disciplined by
chrony against one node of the fleet.
cards.front:
Name the four properties of this instrument that are measured first-party
rather than imported.
cards.title: The four measured instrument properties
cards.why:
The chapter's framing: the impairment characterisation the reproducibility
literature demands is, for the first time here, first-party rather than
imported from someone else's testbed.

choices: As an established effect — a perfect rank correlation with a significant p-value.
As a STRONG MONOTONE TREND and a lead, not an established effect: the p sits at the attainable floor for five nodes and the result turns on a fraction-of-a-degree separation.
As a null result, since five nodes cannot support inference.
As a confound, since temperature and node identity are collinear.
cards.explanation:
With n = 5 the smallest attainable exact p is what was observed, so
significance here carries almost no information beyond "the ordering was
perfect" — and a perfect ordering across five items is not rare. It is
reported because it SUGGESTS amplitude and phase drift have different
causes, which is a candidate hardware-versus-environment separation for the
recalibration trigger. That is what a lead is: worth following, not worth
citing as an effect.
cards.question:
The phase-drift-versus-temperature rank correlation is perfect across five
nodes with an exact p just under 0.05. How should it be reported?
cards.title: How to state the thermal result honestly

cards.back:
Because the science needs RELATIVE COHERENCE between observers more than it
needs absolute UTC. The nodes carry no real-time clock, so a node boots in
the past and the daemon may STEP its clock inside a session.
cards.front:
Why does the fleet discipline time against one of its own nodes, and what
must every reduction do as a consequence?
cards.title: The clock
cards.why:
Every record therefore carries its own timestamp, and any time-domain
reduction must bin on THAT rather than on when a session was started.
Getting this wrong produces a clock seam that looks like a physical event.

cards.back:
An earlier version asserted both capture paths sustained inter-packet
intervals well below the Doppler-aliasing limit. Running the pre-registered
criteria verbatim across the whole archive showed the rate gate PASSED ZERO
TIMES — every arm, on both bands, delivering a small fraction of the
required rate.
cards.front: State the withdrawn packet-rate claim and the instructive error behind it.
cards.title: The withdrawn claim
cards.why:
The error's origin: a single-node capability benchmark had reported a much
higher sustained aggregate, but that figure is a PASSIVE AMBIENT aggregate
summed over all transmitters in earshot — a different estimand from the
delivered rate of a paced reference scoped to one source. Conflating them
produced headroom that did not exist.

cards.back:
Intel firmware blocks transmit-master operation on 5 GHz through its
Location Aware Regulatory mechanism on every client card; the driver
documents no 5 GHz access-point support, and forcing it past the kernel
crashes the CSI backport. There can be no 5 GHz beacon-illuminated arm on
this hardware, ever.
cards.front:
Why is illumination monitor-mode injection rather than access-point
beaconing, and what does that choice save?
cards.title: Why injection, not beaconing
cards.why:
It saves the PAIRED-BAND CONTRAST, which is the strongest control the
thesis has: the same paced reference on both bands in the same room gives a
true negative control for anything specific to the crowded 2.4 GHz band.
An access-point illuminator cannot produce a paired-band design at all.

choices: Clock drift, because the nodes have no real-time clock.

LOST FRAMES. Computed over all arrivals, a coefficient of variation on inter-arrival gaps is dominated by the gaps that missing frames create — so it restates the delivery shortfall the first gate already measures.
Thermal throttling, because throttled nodes drop frames irregularly.
Channel congestion, which is already logged separately.
cards.explanation:
Among frames that ACTUALLY ARRIVED, inter-arrival regularity is excellent —
the injector is metronomic to a fraction of a per cent on a quiet band. The
irregularity the gate measured was the holes, not the timing. The
consequence is a caution about the gate itself: a pass on it must not be
read as independent evidence that the time axis is Doppler-grade. One audit
retired two gates' interpretations at once.
cards.question:
The pre-registered jitter gate turned out to be measuring something else.
What, and why?
cards.title: The gate that was measuring the wrong thing

cards.back:
Delivery is governed by the COMPETING CHANNEL FILL, not by the commanded
rate. A high commanded rate against a quiet channel delivers near-perfectly
with a sub-point fleet spread, while a low commanded rate against a busy
one delivers far worse with a spread of tens of points. The fill itself
swings across a large range on timescales of tens of seconds.
cards.front:
What does the rate ladder establish, and what does it force into every
analysis?
cards.title: The rate ladder's finding
cards.why:
Two consequences: two arms captured at different times are NOT COMPARABLE
on delivery, and channel fill must be logged as a covariate for every
analysis window. The evaluation chapter consumes this table as a tier-two
bound.

cards.back:
The DELIVERED FRACTION of a commanded probe, and the inter-receiver spread
of that fraction — around a dozen points between receivers hearing the same
transmitter on the same channel.
cards.front:
Which measured quantity does the thesis believe the CSI sensing literature
does not report, and why can it not?
cards.title: The unreported quantity
cards.why:
No corpus paper reports it, and none operates a synchronous multi-receiver
array that COULD see it. That is the sense in which the instrument is a
contribution rather than plumbing: the remedy the literature prescribes for
irregular sampling was formed on single monitors at far lower rates, and
whether it survives this spread is an open methodological question this
instrument can answer.

cards.back:
A receiver decoded almost all of an injector transmitting well outside its
passband, with ambient composition proving the two cells sat on different
channels.
cards.front:
What did the two-cell rehearsal find about channel separation, and why does
it happen?
cards.title: Cross-channel leakage
cards.why:
Because a transmit spectral mask specifies RELATIVE attenuation, and at
room scale the absolute out-of-band level still clears the decoding floor
for low-rate OFDM. Any simultaneous within-band comparison on a compact
array is therefore contaminated by construction, and leakage is the first
quantity a multi-channel arm must measure.

choices: Deployed and capturing, with sub-3-metre positional accuracy inside the collector hull.
Controllers verified present and healthy on every node, scanner role deployed and deliberately left switched off — and the project has NEVER captured a real Bluetooth observation.
Absent — the Pi 5 has no Bluetooth controller.
Deployed but disabled pending a data-protection assessment.
cards.explanation:
Every element of the first option is a correction the chapter explicitly
owes: there are no beacons broadcasting a custom protocol, no
collector-role nodes doing trilateration, and the sub-3-metre figure is
IMPORTED from the literature, never a measured property of this deployment.
The third option is the belief that cost two days and was wrong. The
scanner is off on principle: starting a capture is an experimental act and
must not be a side effect of deployment.
cards.question: What is the honest status of the Bluetooth substrate?
cards.title: The BLE substrate, stated bluntly

cards.back:
The inspection tooling could not enumerate symlink-only kernel class
directories, and the attribute being probed is one modern kernels no longer
expose. Neither absence was evidence.
cards.front:
A belief that the fleet had no Bluetooth controller rested on two
independent-looking observations with one shared cause. What was it, and
what rule follows?
cards.title: The two-day methodological lesson
cards.why:
The rule is general: never conclude a device is absent from an empty
listing. Probe a KNOWN-PRESENT SIBLING first as a control on the tool, then
read an attribute every device is guaranteed to have.

cards.back:
Because the device-activity channel supplies a device-count reference that
does not depend on the Bluetooth radio AT ALL — the transmitter census and
the delivery deficit are already in every capture.
cards.front:
Given the Bluetooth substrate is unproven, why is the architecture not
blocked?
cards.title: Why the device-activity channel matters architecturally
cards.why:
So the calibration architecture retains a route to its anchor while the
Bluetooth substrate is unproven. This is also exactly why the thesis
generalises from "BLE" to "device-count channel": the category survives the
failure of one instance.

cards.back:
It replaces scattered configuration — shapefiles of uncertain provenance,
config files duplicating corridor lengths, and researcher memory encoding
door-to-sensor assignments — with a single query-accessible source of truth
consumed identically by simulation, inference and calibration.
cards.front:
What does the PostGIS substrate replace, and what is the one unusual choice
in its design?
cards.title: The spatial substrate
cards.why:
The unusual choice: all geometry is stored in CENTIMETRES under a custom
spatial reference, which eliminates the floating-point drift that
accumulates when metre-resolution projections meet sub-metre placement
decisions. It is in daily use — several floors and hundreds of cells
migrated, and the deployment floor is scan-native rather than
CAD-approximated.

cards.back:
A pedestrian-dynamics engine exposing a Python API that couples directly to
the PostGIS geometry; a trajectory-analytics layer computing density,
velocity and continuity residuals over tessellated measurement regions; and
a GPU differentiable ray tracer ingesting the same 3D mesh and returning
channel impulse responses per agent position.
cards.front:
Name the three simulation tools and the one property that made the stack
work.
cards.title: Why these three simulators
cards.why:
They share a COMMON COORDINATE SYSTEM anchored to the PostGIS substrate,
which minimises glue infrastructure and keeps the pipeline reproducible.
The chapter also stresses what is not established: whether ray-traced
channels resemble captures from the deployed nodes is a validation TARGET,
not a property.

cards.back:
Fleet configuration is declarative and under version control, so "the fleet
was in this state during this session" is answerable from the repository
rather than from memory. And capture sessions carry sidecar provenance —
profile, channel, band, injector configuration, per-session counters —
WRITTEN AT CAPTURE TIME rather than reconstructed.
cards.front:
Two properties of the repository arrangement make claims auditable after
the fact. Name them.
cards.title: The reproducibility property
cards.why:
Written-at-capture-time is the load-bearing half. A provenance record
reconstructed later is a reconstruction, and it cannot settle a dispute
about what actually happened.

cards.back:
Signal extraction (amplitude, phase, Doppler, RSSI); learning paradigm
(classical ML, deep supervised, transfer and few-shot, self- and
semi-supervised); deployment topology (bistatic versus multistatic,
single- versus multi-link, near- versus far-field); and target granularity
(presence, count, localisation, activity).
cards.front:
Name the four axes of the CSI sensing taxonomy, and state the property that
makes them a taxonomy rather than a list.
cards.title: The four axes
cards.why:
They are largely INDEPENDENT — a system's choice of front-end, learning
paradigm, topology and granularity can be combined freely. That is what
lets the taxonomy locate any paper as a point in a space rather than sort
it into a bucket.

choices: As a ranking — the lowest reported MAE identifies the best system.
As a structured INVENTORY: reporting dimensions are aligned but the metrics are not harmonised, so the entries cannot be directly ranked.
As evidence that ESP32 platforms outperform commodity NICs.
As a meta-analysis whose pooled estimate bounds achievable accuracy.
cards.explanation:
Descriptive normalisation aligns people range, hardware, environment count
and reported metric — it does not make MAE, discrete occupancy-level
accuracy and combined counting-accuracy-plus-latency scores commensurable.
Saying so is not a hedge; it is what licenses the chapter's actual finding,
which is structural rather than numerical: NO system in the table reports
cross-site generalisation under controlled conditions, which makes
scalability-under-transfer an open empirical question.
cards.question:
The chapter tabulates representative CSI crowd-counting systems. How should
the table be read?
cards.title: Reading the comparison table

cards.back:
The pattern that counting accuracy degrades as occupancy grows — one
surveyed system reports error rising between five and ten people, and
another shows subcarrier-level features saturating in discriminative power
as occupancy rises.
cards.front:
What is the "accuracy-versus-scalability ceiling", and how strong is the
evidence for it in this chapter?
cards.title: The accuracy–scalability ceiling
cards.why:
The chapter is careful about strength: a directionally consistent
degradation in one system HINTS at a ceiling, and whether it is a
field-level regularity or an isolated data point cannot be confirmed from
a single system alone. That caution is why the thesis later derives the
saturation rather than citing it.

cards.back:
Domain-invariant feature extraction; virtual or augmented sample
generation; transfer learning with limited fine-tuning; few-shot adaptation
from a handful of target examples; and big-data coverage, where
generalisation emerges from sheer training diversity.
cards.front:
Name the five recurring families the literature marshals against
cross-domain shift.
cards.title: The five adaptation families
cards.why:
All five presuppose access to labelled or at least COLLECTED target-domain
data. That shared premise is what the newer label-free thread questions —
and it is also, in the end, what this thesis declines to question, because
two anchors beat every label-free alternative it tested.

cards.back:
It promises to dispense with per-site labelled data entirely — pretrain on
abundant unlabelled CSI, then adapt on-device with lightweight
self-calibration. The motivation is economic: even few-shot and transfer
still require collected target samples.
cards.front:
What does the self-supervised / on-device self-calibration thread promise,
and what two cautions does the chapter attach?
cards.title: The label-free frontier
cards.why:
Caution one: on-device self-calibration presumes channel statistics are
stable enough BETWEEN updates to be tracked, which strains under genuine
non-stationarity. Caution two: mature exemplars are scarce, so the
reliability of unsupervised adaptation is largely unvalidated at scale.
The thread nonetheless foreshadows this thesis's angle — substituting a
cheap SCHEDULED EXTERNAL REFERENCE for unsupervised self-correction.

choices: There is not enough public CSI data.
There is no canonical, hardware-agnostic representation — the CSI tensor is inseparable from the chipset, subcarrier layout, extraction preprocessing and task definition that produced it.
Researchers do not release their code.
Occupancy labels are too expensive to collect accurately.
cards.explanation:
Computer vision has the RGB pixel array — a substrate any dataset and any
model share. WiFi sensing has nothing equivalent, so public datasets
diverge along every dimension at once. The chapter is explicit that the
problem is not a shortage of data: curated collections exist, and they are
themselves heterogeneous in chipset, bandwidth and labelling convention.
Progress is throttled by the missing representation, not by an algorithmic
ceiling.
cards.question: The chapter diagnoses the reproducibility deficit. What is its root cause?
cards.title: Why WiFi sensing has no ImageNet

cards.back:
A standardised WLAN Sensing procedure — sensing measurement instances,
negotiation frames and reporting primitives — so compliant access points
deliver channel-sounding reports on demand alongside normal traffic, in a
HARDWARE-AGNOSTIC measurement exchange.
cards.front: What does IEEE 802.11bf promise, and what is its status?
cards.title: The standardisation horizon
cards.why:
Status matters: the amendment is in final ratification and early
commercialisation, so vendor-portable interoperable CSI sensing is a
PROSPECTIVE capability, not a deployed substrate. The thesis's experimental
work runs on pre-standard commodity hardware and says so.

cards.back:
Because one waveform serves two ends, there is a fundamental
sensing-versus-communication trade-off: gains in sensing accuracy are paid
for in communication rate and vice versa.
cards.front:
What does ISAC theory bound, and what is the concrete consequence for this
thesis?
cards.title: The ISAC trade-off
cards.why:
Commodity-WiFi crowd sensing operates in a band whose PRIMARY OBLIGATION is
communication, so it inherits a bounded sensing budget. The point is not
the derivation — that belongs to information theory — but the expectation
it sets: attainable sensing fidelity is principled and finite, not
arbitrarily improvable by a better estimator.

cards.back:
Cross-environment domain generalisation; non-stationary interference and
channel drift over time; and the scaling of accuracy with crowd density
and deployment size.
cards.front: Name the three challenge clusters the chapter distils.
cards.title: The three challenge clusters
cards.why:
Note that they are not independent of each other, and the thesis exploits
that: the drift cluster is what makes a RECALIBRATION POLICY a research
question rather than an engineering detail, and the generalisation cluster
is what makes a local anchor worth its cost.

choices: Recalibration cost → BLE augmentation and CSI sensing; temporal structure under occlusion → crowd modelling and fusion; drift-triggered scheduling → fusion and evaluation.
Recalibration cost → evaluation; temporal structure → CSI sensing; drift scheduling → system design.
All three gaps are closed in the evaluation chapter, since that is where the measurements are.
Recalibration cost → crowd modelling; temporal structure → BLE augmentation; drift scheduling → implementation.
cards.explanation:
Recalibration is prohibitively expensive because existing approaches need
dense labelled CSI per deployment — closed by exploiting co-located
device-count infrastructure, with the accompanying hardware-versus-layout
shift hypothesis tested in the CSI chapter. Temporal structure under
occlusion is where the thesis takes the natural remedy the literature
suggests, tests it, and REPORTS THAT IT FAILS, relocating the exploitable
structure to state-space filtering and spectral features. Drift-triggered
scheduling is derived in the fusion chapter and pre-registered for
measurement in evaluation.
cards.question:
The chapter maps three addressable gaps onto contributions. Which mapping
is correct?
cards.title: The three gaps and their chapters

cards.back:
It announces a NEGATIVE as the contribution. The chapter says the thesis
takes the remedy the literature suggests — a density-continuity prior
grounded in conservation-of-mass reasoning — puts it to a pre-registered
test, and reports that it does not beat generic smoothing on indoor
geometry.
cards.front:
The second research gap is stated in a way most literature chapters would
not risk. What is unusual about it?
cards.title: The honest gap in the gap map
cards.why:
A literature chapter that promises to close a gap and then closes it by
showing the obvious approach fails is making a stronger claim than one that
promises success, because it forecloses a design rather than adding one.

cards.back:
Measured results; a deployed instrument and its characterisation; an
architecture; and documented negatives.
cards.front: The contributions divide into four families. Name them.
cards.title: The four contribution families
cards.why:
The fourth is the unusual one, and the chapter defends it in a clause worth
memorising: the thesis counts the negatives as contributions BECAUSE each
one retires a design the field would otherwise keep proposing.

cards.back:
On a pooled public corpus of seven environments and two hardware platforms,
CSI counting transfers as a PARTIAL-POOLING model: the count-to-variability
mechanism is sign-stable everywhere, its scale is platform-stratified, and
two labelled anchors per new environment recover most of the transfer loss.
cards.front:
State the anchored-calibration law and the sentence that makes it a
contribution rather than an observation.
cards.title: The first measured contribution
cards.why:
The sentence: local labels are not a CONVENIENCE but a MATHEMATICAL
NECESSITY, and very few of them suffice. Four independent label-free
alternatives lost under pre-registered kill lines, for a reason
domain-adaptation theory names in advance — the dominant error is a
session-structural offset no unlabelled objective can identify.

cards.back:
Under environment shift the point-count contract degrades on band ranked
probability score while the discrete distributional contract does not move,
and its stated confidences become MORE honest where the point contract's
become less.
cards.front:
State the distributional output contract's result in one sentence, and its
one-line consequence for what the thesis reports.
cards.title: The second measured contribution
cards.why:
Consequence: the thesis reports P(N = k), not a point estimate. Wrapped in
Mondrian conformal prediction the same estimator certifies coverage at
usable width in-environment, and its zero-shot collapse RE-DERIVES the
local-anchor requirement distribution-free.

choices: That commodity hardware is sufficient for CSI sensing at scale.
That delivery, loss and channel occupancy are MEASURANDS of a sensing instrument rather than deployment plumbing — and that a multi-receiver array is what makes them visible at all.
That ten nodes give better spatial coverage than one.
That the fleet is reproducible because its configuration is version-controlled.
cards.explanation:
The claim has two halves and the second is what makes it a contribution
rather than an engineering report. Quantities the CSI literature does not
report — the delivered fraction of a commanded probe audited across a whole
archive, an inter-receiver delivery spread across nine synchronous
observers, delivery governed by competing load rather than commanded rate,
cross-channel leakage at close range, two receiver fault classes with no
upstream detector — are invisible to a single-monitor methodology. The
array is what makes them measurable.
cards.question:
What is the METHODOLOGICAL claim behind counting the measurement instrument
as a contribution?
cards.title: The instrument as a contribution

cards.back:
The calibration loop is ONE STATE-SPACE ESTIMATOR. The staleness-weighted
fusion of an intermittent absolute reference with a continuous relative
sensor is the filter's gain trajectory, and the recalibration trigger is
sequential change-point detection on the filter's innovation.
cards.front:
State the architectural contribution in one sentence, and name the two
mechanisms it unifies.
cards.title: The architectural contribution
cards.why:
And the honesty clause that travels with it: the evidence is in-silico and
labelled as such, with the powered replication's demotions applied, so the
demonstrated payoff of the drift-triggered controller is a
calibration-budget saving at a small accuracy cost — NOT accuracy parity.

cards.back:
As a CATEGORY: BLE advertisements and ambient device activity are two
INSTANCES with near-orthogonal failure modes to CSI. And the
device-to-person ratio is a jointly identified latent whose sufficient
statistic the participant protocol measures rather than assumes.
cards.front: How does the conclusion state what the calibration reference IS?
cards.title: The reference is a category
cards.why:
Generalising from the instance to the category is what keeps the
architecture alive while the Bluetooth substrate remains unproven. It is
also a better claim: an architecture that needs one specific radio is more
fragile than one that needs a device-count channel.

cards.back:
A continuity-equation physics prior on crowd density, specified, tested
across three independent in-silico testbeds, and refuted TWICE —
closure-invariantly. A purely statistical anytime-valid drift trigger that
fires on certified-empty rooms and cannot alone govern recalibration
spending. And a delay-spread band contrast reported by an early experiment
card that died under re-reduction, taking with it every
multipath-richness argument the narrow-bandwidth hardware could have
carried.
cards.front: Name the three documented negatives the conclusion lists.
cards.title: The three documented negatives
cards.why:
Each is reproducible from committed reductions, and each REDIRECTED the
design toward the architecture the thesis now defends. A negative that
changed nothing would not be a contribution.

cards.back:
PARTIALLY ANSWERED, with the measured half favourable and the in-vivo half
designed and pending. Settled: a WiFi capture cannot substitute for a BLE
receiver, because the advertising channels fall outside every 2.4 GHz WiFi
channel's occupied band by construction — so the reference needs its own
radio, which the fleet carries. And anchor quality reduces to one scalar,
the product of detection rate and carriage penetration.
cards.front: Give RQ1's verdict, its settled half, and its open half.
cards.title: RQ1's verdict
cards.why:
Open: a first-party in-vivo census validated against scheduled occupancy —
the opening arm of the pre-registered campaign. The participant protocol
measures the scalar by construction: one phase sets penetration to one, the
next makes it a covariate.

cards.back:
ANSWERED ON PUBLIC REAL DATA, with first-party confirmation pending.
Accuracy: the two-anchor result against its oracle. What survives an
environment change: the feature TYPE — kinematic and distributional
features transfer where fingerprint-like features collapse, and hardware
shift dominates layout shift. Degradation over time: the empty-room
amplitude drift floor of the deployed instrument.
cards.front: Give RQ2's verdict and its three components.
cards.title: RQ2's verdict
cards.why:
Note the qualifier the conclusion attaches to the band advantage: it is
real on the corpus, but it is a property of the VARIANCE FEATURE and
conditional on channel congestion — not an intrinsic property of the radio.
And the drift floor's meaning is negative: occupancy sensing is NOT
drift-limited overnight.

cards.back:
**The prior: NO.** Mass conservation imposed as a training-time regulariser
does not beat generic smoothing on indoor geometry. The evidence is a
mismatched-closure ablation: a physically correct velocity closure, a
constant one, and an ANTI-PHYSICAL one all produced the same high-density
error, while a plain smoothness prior with no conservation content beat all
three. A term whose benefit survives inverting the law it encodes was never
acting as physics. Tested across three independent in-silico testbeds with
pre-registered margins, and refuted twice.

**The relocation: YES, and this is the positive half.** On the identical
data, a quasi-static amplitude statistic explains almost none of the count
variance while an intra-frame fading feature multiplies the fit several
times over. The count lives in the channel's TEMPORAL and SPECTRAL
structure. The eigenvalue analysis then ties the saturation to a detection
budget set by measurement geometry rather than by the room.

**What survives of the continuum commitment** is the density-field TARGET —
estimating a field rather than a roster — not a fluid prior.
cards.front:
RQ3 asked whether a continuum crowd model can constrain CSI-to-density
inference, and where the recoverable count signal lives. Answer it in full
— both halves.
cards.title: RQ3's verdict
cards.why:
The shape of this answer is worth as much as its content. The question was
asked in two parts and it is answered in two parts, one negative and one
positive, from the SAME experiment. A refutation that also tells you where
to look next is a result; one that only closes a door is a setback.

cards.back:
DESIGNED AND BOUNDED, NOT YET NUMBERED. Its STRUCTURE is answered: measured
drift beats a fixed schedule (on easy environments every scheduled
recalibration setting is harmful), a purely statistical trigger is refuted
as a sole governor by the certified-empty measurement, and the deployable
trigger is referenced disagreement with a magnitude gate.
cards.front:
Give RQ4's verdict verbatim in structure: what is answered, and what is
not.
cards.title: RQ4's verdict
cards.why:
What is not answered is the deployment pair (T*, ε), which is the labelled
result slot of the pre-registered drift study. The error envelope is
honestly reported by construction — the distributional contract with
conformal coverage — and the held-out-environment half is answered on
public corpora by the two-anchor recovery.

cards.back:
Every certified occupancy is zero, so all first-party occupancy claims
await the campaign. Tier-one results ride on public corpora, so a
cross-dataset instrumentation confound persists. The anchor evidence is two
oracle anchors on one pooled corpus. Fusion and trigger evidence is
in-silico. The instrument carries declared risks — a delivery spread not
yet shown harmless to per-link features, two fault classes with recent
detectors, and a WiFi channel that was a fixed setting rather than a
controlled variable for the project's whole history. The BLE substrate has
never produced a labelled in-vivo session. And the participant instrument's
positional truth is bounded.
cards.front:
Name the limitations a careful reader should weigh, in the order the
chapter gives them.
cards.title: The limitations, as a list
cards.why:
The last one has a concrete consequence: LiDAR meshes register to the
surveyed floor at decimetre-to-metre residuals in live conditions, so
ground truth is anchored on SCHEDULED, WALL-CLOCK-STAMPED occupancy rather
than on reconstructed positions.

choices: It is reported as resolved in favour of the simulation.

It is reported as OPEN and as WEAKENING the measured headline rather than supporting it: two independent simulations give one sign of correlation where the single real walk capture measured the opposite on the same statistic and geometry.
It is reported in a footnote, since one capture cannot overturn two simulations.
It is reported as a limitation of the walk capture's registration accuracy.
cards.explanation:
Stating that your own evidence points the wrong way, and saying so in the
direction that costs you rather than the direction that excuses you, is the
single most defensible move available in a limitations section. The
temptation the third option describes is real — two simulations against one
capture LOOKS like a majority — and the thesis declines it, because a real
capture and a simulation are not two votes of equal weight.
cards.question:
The limitations report one sim-to-real disagreement as open. What is
unusual about how it is reported?
cards.title: The open disagreement

cards.back:
The channel as a CONTROLLED VARIABLE — a within-band congestion control
deciding whether the band rule is about wavelength or about load.
Simultaneous multi-channel sensing on ten independent radios, provided
cross-channel leakage is bounded first. Occupancy validation of the
device-activity channel against the faculty timetable — a zero-cost label
source for a whole semester. And the dual-use question, analysable on
corpora the thesis already holds.
cards.front:
Name the four future directions, and say what distinguishes the nearest
work from all of them.
cards.title: The four future directions
cards.why:
The nearest work is SCHEDULED, NOT SPECULATIVE: the pre-registered in-vivo
campaign fills the labelled result slots of the evaluation chapter, and its
second phase repeats the protocol with partial app penetration to measure
the device-to-person statistic in the wild.

cards.back:
The ethics posture of the supporting appendix commits the released dataset
to make the dual-use analysis REPRODUCIBLE RATHER THAN CONVENIENT.
cards.front:
The dual-use direction carries a commitment about the released dataset.
What is it, and why is the wording pointed?
cards.title: The ethics commitment in future work
cards.why:
The distinction is deliberate. A dataset released to make an attack easy is
irresponsible; a dataset released so an unwelcome analysis can be checked is
the opposite. Committing to the second in the closing paragraph — where a
reader is deciding what kind of researcher wrote this — is a placement
choice, not an accident.

cards.back:
The empirical density–speed (or density–flow) relation: walking speed
falls as density rises, from free-flow (~1.34 m/s) toward standstill near
jam density. It is the macroscopic calibration target every microscopic
model must reproduce.
cards.front: What is the pedestrian fundamental diagram (FD)?
cards.title: Fundamental diagram

cards.back:
Force-based (Social Force: agents driven by attractive goal +repulsive
interaction forces), velocity-based (Collision-Free Speed Model: speed
chosen directly from headway), cellular automata (discrete grid), and
anticipation/vision-based models (AVM). Our engine uses JuPedSim's CFSM
on the agenda path.
cards.front: Name the main microscopic pedestrian-model families.
cards.title: Model families

cards.back:
Speed = min(v0, headway-limited speed): the agent moves at desired speed
unless the gap to the next agent divided by time gap T dictates slower.
T IS the fundamental-diagram slope b — larger T = more cautious/comfortable
spacing. JuPedSim default T = 1.0 s ≈ 2× Seyfried's fitted b ≈ 0.56 s, a
defensible low-motivation indoor regime but NOT "Seyfried-grounded."
cards.front:
How does the Collision-Free Speed Model set an agent's speed, and what is
the meaning of its T parameter?
cards.title: CFSM speed rule

cards.back:
r = 0.20 m — the one parameter both consumed by the engine and
literature-confirmed (Maury–Venel 2r contact constraint; Seyfried
fundamental-diagram intercept 0.36–0.40 m).
cards.front:
What agent radius do we parameterise, what grounds it, and why is
shrinking it to make a floor walkable a cheat?
cards.title: Grounded parameters
cards.why:
Drifting it to 0.10 m is a geometry-cheat: it buys a passing gate by
making bodies smaller than bodies. When a gate fails at free-flow
density, fix the SCENE, not the radius.

cards.back:
v0 = 1.34 m/s — the Weidmann central value, and the free-flow speed the
Weidmann closure relaxes toward.
cards.front:
What free-flow desired speed do we give agents, and which nearby figure
is the trap?
cards.title: Desired speed
cards.why:
The 1.5–1.6 m/s figures that appear in speed-prediction papers are
congested fundamental-diagram asymptotes, not free-flow desired speeds.
Quoting one as v0 mixes two different quantities.

choices: 0.6 m standard single-pedestrian occupancy (HCM 2010); 0.4 m absolute passability floor
0.9 m ADA wheelchair clearance; 0.6 m floor
1.2 m bidirectional flow width; 0.8 m floor
0.5 m shoulder width; 0.3 m floor
cards.explanation:
0.6 m = HCM-2010 single-pedestrian occupancy (hassanpour2021); 0.4 m =
single-file passability floor (ma2025). Protect the swept corridor
THROUGH the door, oriented — a perpendicular obstacle beside the jamb is
a harmless column effect.
cards.question: What door-clearance standards ground our furniture placer's F-Space rule?
cards.title: Doors

cards.back:
Strategic (activity choice) → tactical (route/destination sequencing) →
operational (locomotion). Real indoor movement is activity/destination-
based with required dwells (hospital laser-scanner data: global
least-cost route + local correction), so origin→exit through-traffic
misses most of the occupancy structure. Our agenda/FSM engine models the
strategic layer explicitly.
cards.front:
What is the three-level model of pedestrian behaviour and why does
through-traffic fail as an indoor model?
cards.title: Strategic–tactical–operational

cards.back:
Essentially no. Raw arms differed (KS D = 0.40, p = 4e-4), but matching
headcount collapsed it: resampled D = 0.26 (p = 0.056), matched-by-
construction D = 0.24 (p = 0.095), and at 20 seeds the effect SHRANK to
D = 0.135 — the fingerprint was headcount. A counting model robust to
occupancy-distribution shift absorbs the behaviour difference.
cards.front:
Does agent BEHAVIOUR (reactive FSMs vs scripted itineraries) leave a CSI
fingerprint beyond headcount?
cards.title: Behaviour vs headcount
cards.why: Textbook example of a vanishing effect under proper matching + power.

choices: The effect is tiny; more power SHRANK the estimate and significance came only from sample size — report effect size, not the p-value
The effect became real at 20 seeds — significance confirms it
The test was invalid at 5 seeds and valid at 20
KS distance always decreases with n, so nothing can be concluded
cards.explanation:
A shrinking effect estimate with growing n plus a barely-significant p is
the signature of a negligible effect made "significant" by power. ~86%
distribution overlap. Also: cite the per-(link,seed) variance KS, not the
over-powered pooled residual KS whose observations aren't independent.
cards.question:
In the flat-day matched-arm study, quadrupling seeds moved KS D from 0.24
to 0.135 while p crossed under 0.05. What is the correct reading?
cards.title: Power lesson

cards.back:
Refuted in-silico and shelved (candidate → deferred). The continuity gain
was FD-agnostic and plain temporal smoothing beat it; the directed-flow
probe closed the last open door (strong directed flow did not rescue it).
It stays out of the thesis core — an honest cut.
cards.front: What happened to the "crowd as fluid" continuity-prior hypothesis?
cards.title: Continuity prior

cards.back:
jupedsim-runner (JuPedSim CFSM locomotion under our agenda/FSM behaviour
engine — walk-notebook), and pedpy-analyser (FD/flow analysis of
trajectories). They form the pedestrian class beside the channel class
(sionna-csi-runner); coupled experiments chain walk-notebook →

cards.front:
Which pedestrian-dynamics tools does the platform host, and what does
each do?
cards.title: Simulator roster

cards.back:
A first-order model with identical agents is over-smooth and prone to
symmetry-locked gridlock (agents mirror each other indefinitely).
Per-agent v0 draws (e.g. N(1.34, 0.2)) break the symmetry — heterogeneity
is a modelling necessity, not decoration.
cards.front:
Why does a deterministic single-v0 crowd model misbehave, and what is the
fix?
cards.title: Heterogeneity

cards.back:
Occlusion behaved: a body crossing a ray drops on-ray amplitude by tens
of decibels and variance monotonicity is perfect. What did not behave is
the inference — the observability paradox held, so a well-modelled
forward channel does not make the inverse problem easy.
cards.front:
In the flat-day coupled simulation, which half of the physics behaved and
which half did not?
cards.title: Occlusion physics
cards.why:
This is the standing shape of the sim corpus: forward physics is the
trustworthy part, and every difficulty lives on the inverse side.

cards.back:
Crowd density: how many people stand on a square metre, written as a field
ρ(x, t) — a number attached to every point of the floor and every instant,
not one number for the room. Units are pedestrians per square metre,
written ped/m².

It is a FIELD, and that is not a technicality. One number for a room hides
the doorway where everyone is standing, and the doorway is where the
interesting physics happens.
cards.example:
Our own measurement room, so the numbers are not abstract. The library
ground-floor space is roughly 8 m × 6 m, so about 48 m² of floor.

At 0.5 ped/m² that is **24 people** — a quiet reading room, and you would
walk through without changing your path. At Weidmann's capacity density,
about 1.75 ped/m², it is **84 people** and the room is moving as fast as it
ever will in total. At the 5.4 ped/m² jam density it would be **259**, and
nobody is going anywhere.

Our own certified-empty sessions are all at exactly 0.0, which is both the
cleanest number in the corpus and the reason the calibration spine is still
at plausible rather than measured.

figures.caption: What the values feel like. The capacity and jam figures are Weidmann's fitted metastudy values as reported in the vault's crowd corpus; the empirical capacity density across independent studies is a RANGE, 1.3 to 2.3, not a constant.
rows: certified empty — verified, with a live receiver
quiet corridor; you do not adjust your path

cards.front: ρ — what is it, in what units, and what do its values feel like?
cards.title: Density
cards.why:
It is the thesis's estimation TARGET, and that survived the refutation of
the physics prior. The continuum framing earns its place by fixing what a
radio can hope to recover — aggregate flux, not individual paths — not by
supplying a constraint.

cards.back:
The pedestrian velocity field: the mean velocity shared by everyone in an
infinitesimal volume, under the homogeneous-velocity assumption. Same
shape as the density field — a value at every point and instant — but a
VECTOR at each point rather than a number, because a velocity has a
direction.

The homogeneous-velocity assumption is doing real work and is worth saying
aloud: it asserts that everybody in a small patch of floor is moving the
same way. It is what lets a crowd be written as a fluid at all.
cards.example:
Free walking speed is one of the best-measured quantities in the field, and
it is not one number. Measured speeds are distributed roughly normally
about **1.30 m/s with a standard deviation of 0.21 m/s** — and the mean
depends on who you are walking with: an isolated individual averages
**1.38 m/s**, a group of six averages **1.10 m/s**.

Now the sensing consequence. A library reading room has people walking in
every direction and standing still for long stretches, so the MEAN velocity
over a patch is close to zero while individuals are plainly moving. The
field is nearly zero and its divergence is noise — which is exactly the
regime where the conservation-law prior had nothing to add, and the reason
the refutation was about geometry rather than about arithmetic.

figures.caption: Both patches hold four moving people. The corridor's mean velocity is large and its direction is meaningful; the reading room's mean is near zero and says nothing about whether anyone moved. Same density, same motion, opposite observability.

cards.front: v (or u) — what is it, and why is it the problem child?
cards.title: Velocity field
cards.why:
Its unobservability is what defeated the continuity prior. In
low-directed-flow indoor geometry the velocity field carries too little
signal for the divergence term to be informative, so the physics penalty
is effectively inert.

cards.example:
A 2 m wide library doorway, using Weidmann's fit at three densities.

At 0.5 ped/m²: speed 1.30 m/s, flow 0.65 per metre per second, so the
doorway passes about **2.6 people a second**. At capacity, 1.75 ped/m²:
speed 0.70, flow 1.23, so about **2.5 a second** — no better, at three
times the density. At 4.0 ped/m²: speed 0.16, flow 0.63, about **1.3 a
second**, half the rate at eight times the crowd.

That is the whole argument for measuring density rather than counting heads
at the door: the door's throughput is the same at 0.5 and at 1.75, and only
the density says which of those two rooms you are standing in.
cards.explanation:
Pedestrian flow, also called flux: how many people cross a one-metre line
per second. It is density times speed, and nothing more — but because speed
itself falls as density rises, the product does something neither factor
does alone.

**Concave** means bending downward: the curve lies below every straight
line drawn between two of its own points. The practical content of that one
word is that the function has a single interior maximum, so there is one
best density and both sides of it are worse. Convex would be the opposite,
bending upward — and a convex flow curve would mean packing people in
always helped, which is false.

Why the peak exists at all is not obvious, and the crowd-physics literature
is careful about it. If everybody walked at exactly the same constant
speed, flow WOULD just rise linearly to the jam point. The turnover comes
from the variability BETWEEN and WITHIN walkers: differing speeds produce
what the literature calls repulsive collisions, the same mechanism that
produces shocks in traffic flow.

For this thesis the shape carries a design consequence. Throughput past
capacity falls, so a building's busiest moment is not its highest-density
moment — and an occupancy estimator reporting only "how many" cannot tell
the operator which side of the peak the room is on.

fields.meaning: pedestrian flow or flux — people crossing a metre of line per second
local density in ped/m²
the speed–density closure; Weidmann's fitted form
free walking speed in m/s, the fit's asymptote at zero density
jam density in ped/m² — the fit's upper limit, where speed hits zero

figures.caption: Concavity, drawn. The dashed line is what flow would do if crowding never slowed anyone: straight up for ever. The real curve bends BELOW every one of its own chords, turns over at about 1.75 ped/m², and comes back to zero at the jam density. Computed from Weidmann's fitted form as reported in the vault's crowd corpus, not measured here.
figures.y_label: q — flow (ped per metre per second)

cards.question:
q — define it, say where it peaks, and define "concave" while you are
there.
cards.reading:
Flow is density times speed, and speed is the fitted falling function of
density, so flow rises, turns over, and falls back to zero.
cards.title: Flow

cards.example:
Two experiments in the vault's own crowd corpus fitted Weidmann's model to
the same quantity and did not agree, which is the honest version of what
"site-calibratable" means.

In a corridor the least-squares fit gave a time gap of about **0.85 s** and
a free speed of **1.50 m/s**. At a bottleneck, the same fit on the same
apparatus gave **0.49 s** and **1.64 m/s**. Pedestrian size came out almost
identical either way, 0.64 m against 0.61 m.

Read that as the calibration statement it is: the body does not change
between the corridor and the doorway, and the behaviour does. Any
deployment that imports one venue's closure into another venue is importing
the behaviour along with it.
cards.explanation:
The speed–density closure, also called the fundamental diagram: speed
expressed as a single-valued function of local density.

What it is FOR is arithmetic, not realism. The conservation law relates
density and velocity, which is two unknowns in one equation — unsolvable.
The closure supplies the second relation by ASSERTING that speed is a
function of density alone, which turns the pair into something integrable.
It is the price of the continuum framing, and it is a real assumption: two
crowds at the same density and different intents walk at different speeds.

It is also the ONLY component the thesis treats as site-calibratable — and
that restriction is deliberate rather than modest. The eikonal direction
field, the obstacle geometry, the corridor widths and the exit boundary
conditions all change across venues too, and every one of them has to be
re-specified separately. A thesis that claimed the closure was the only
thing needing re-fitting would be claiming the geometry travels, which it
does not.

fields.meaning: free walking speed — 1.34 m/s in Weidmann's fit
jam density — 5.4 ped/m², where speed reaches zero
shape parameter, 1.913 in the fit: how sharply speed falls
the single-valued speed the model assigns to a density

figures.caption: Scrubbing v₀ shows what site calibration does and does not change. The SHAPE — monotone falling, zero at the jam density — holds across every frame. The level moves, and the measured spread of free speeds across real experiments is about this wide.

a site with slower walkers, v₀ = p
