cards.question:
U(ρ) or f(ρ) — what is it, what is it FOR, and what is the one component
this thesis lets a site re-fit?
cards.reading:
Speed is the free walking speed, reduced by a factor that vanishes as
density approaches the jam density.
cards.title: The closure

cards.back:
The discomfort or cost function of density: how unpleasant a place is to be
in, expressed as a number that rises as it gets more crowded. In Hughes'
continuum model pedestrians are assumed to move so as to minimise the total
cost of their route, so G is what makes a crowd flow AROUND a dense patch
rather than straight through it.

The behaviour it produces is the reason it exists. With no discomfort term
the shortest path always wins and crowds walk into jams. With one, the
route that is slightly longer and much emptier starts winning, which is
what people actually do.
cards.example:
A railway concourse with two staircases: yours is thirty metres away and
packed, the other is fifty metres away and empty. Nobody computes a
functional, and everybody takes the second one anyway — that decision is
what a discomfort term encodes.

Note what is NOT claimed here. This thesis fits no discomfort function and
measures no route choice. G appears so that the model this thesis borrows
from can be stated correctly, and the borrowed vocabulary is marked as
borrowed.

figures.caption: One legitimate choice of discomfort: the reciprocal of the speed the closure allows, which is the time cost of crossing a metre of that floor. It is finite and flat while the room is quiet, then climbs without bound as the jam density approaches. Illustrative — this thesis fits no discomfort function.

cards.front: G(ρ) — what is it, and what behaviour does it produce?
cards.title: Discomfort
cards.why:
Part of the Hughes continuum vocabulary — pedestrians move to minimise a
cost that rises with crowding. It is inherited notation, not a fitted
component of this system.

cards.back:
The cost potential of the continuum crowd model — the eikonal field whose
gradient sets preferred walking direction.

Read it as a landscape. Every point of the floor is assigned a number
saying how expensive it is to reach the exit from there, and everyone walks
DOWNHILL on that landscape. The gradient of φ at a point is the steepest
downhill direction, so the field converts "where is the exit" into a local
instruction available at every point, with no global route planning.
cards.example:
Water on a hillside. Nothing tells a raindrop where the valley is, and every
drop reaches it, because the local slope is enough. An eikonal field is that
hillside computed for a floor plan, with crowding raising the ground where
people are already standing.

The venue dependence is the load-bearing part. Move the same crowd model
into a room with one more doorway and every value of φ changes, because the
cost of every point changed. That is why the thesis calls the closure
site-calibratable and the direction field site-SPECIFIC: one is a curve you
can re-fit from a few observations, the other is a whole field determined by
a floor plan.

figures.caption: The potential as a landscape: cost falls towards the exit, the arrows are its downhill gradient, and a dense patch raises the ground so the arrows bend around it. Change the doorway and every arrow moves.

cards.front: φ — what is it, and what does its gradient decide?
cards.title: Cost potential
cards.why:
Hughes' model augments the continuity equation with exactly this to
determine direction. It is the piece of the spatial problem that does NOT
travel between venues.

cards.back:
The channel frequency response, per subcarrier: the complex coefficient
H(k) the receiver recovers to equalise an OFDM symbol. One complex number
per subcarrier per antenna pair per frame.

Under the narrowband model Y(k) = H(k)X(k) + N(k): the receiver knows the
training symbol X(k), sees what arrived as Y(k), and divides. CSI is
precisely the vector of recovered H(k) over the occupied subcarriers.

What it is NOT: a property of the transmitter, a property of the receiver,
or a measurement of a person. It is a property of the ROOM between them,
contaminated by both radios' imperfections.
cards.example:
The clearest way to feel what H is: send the same known symbol from the
same transmitter twice, once into an empty room and once with a person
standing between the antennas. X is identical both times. Y differs. The
entire difference is H, and the entire content of H is the room.

Our certified-empty sessions are that first half taken seriously: over a
thousand minutes of verified-unoccupied observation with a live-receiver
control, so that the empty-room H is a measurement rather than an
assumption.

figures.caption: Why the sensing is free: every one of these steps happens anyway, for communication. Extracting H is reading a number the receiver already computed, not asking the network for anything.

messages.label: ACK — and Ĥ is normally discarded here

cards.front: H — what is it, over what index, and what is it NOT?
cards.title: Channel response
cards.why:
The receiver has to compute it to demodulate at all, which is why the
sensing signal is free. No extra hardware, no extra transmission, no
cooperation from anyone being measured.

cards.example:
Two receivers, monad03 and monad05, hearing the SAME injected frame on the
same channel at the same instant. Their raw amplitude vectors differ by a
large constant factor, because their gain controls settled differently.

Take the ratio of each to its own median across tones and the two curves
land on top of each other, because the shape was always the same — the
height never was. That is a one-line operation and it is the difference
between an inter-receiver comparison and a comparison of two gain settings.

The same discipline is what makes the delivery spread across those nine
receivers a measurand rather than an artefact: quantities that survive
median-centring are about the room, and quantities that do not are about
the radio.
cards.explanation:
CSI amplitude: the magnitude of the complex channel coefficient, discarding
the phase. It is what almost every CSI sensing paper actually works with,
because phase needs heavy repair and amplitude does not.

The dimensions matter and are usually left vague, so state them. One record
gives you one amplitude per subcarrier per antenna pair: **242 numbers per
pair on a 20 MHz HE channel, 996 at 160 MHz**, against the 56 that most of
the published literature runs on. A second of capture at our measured
608 Hz is therefore roughly 600 of those vectors. Amplitude is a
non-negative real number in the receiver's own units — not watts, not
decibel-milliwatts, not anything with a physical scale attached.

Which is the trap. Amplitude is **relative to the receiver's automatic gain
control**, a circuit whose job is to keep the signal inside the converter's
range by changing how much it amplifies. When it steps, every amplitude in
the record steps with it, and nothing in the record says it happened. So
absolute |H| is not comparable between captures, between receivers, or
sometimes across one capture.

The consequence runs through the whole thesis. Any honest comparison
median-centres amplitude first, which is why the CSI comparison tool
refuses to plot two sources without doing so. And it is why the natural
feature is the mean-scaled coefficient of variation rather than raw
variance: a ratio survives a gain change, a variance does not.

the real and imaginary parts the receiver reports
subcarrier index — 242 of them on a 20 MHz HE frame
median-centred amplitude — the only form comparable between captures

cards.question:
|H| — what exactly is it, what does it look like in real data, and what is
the trap that comes with it?
cards.reading:
Amplitude is the length of the complex channel coefficient; the comparable
version divides it by the median across tones.
cards.title: Amplitude

cards.example:
Same subcarrier, same node, two one-second windows, in the receiver's own
units.

Certified-empty window: mean 0.500, standard deviation 0.010, so
CV = **0.02**. Occupied window: mean 0.480, standard deviation 0.062, so
CV = **0.13**. The mean barely moved — about 4% — and the CV went up more
than sixfold. That asymmetry is the reason variability rather than level is
the counting feature in a room with no dominant direct path.

Now the failure this fixes. Suppose the second window had also seen the
gain control step, scaling every sample by 1.8: mean 0.864, standard
deviation 0.112. The RAW variance is up by a factor of about 125 against
the empty window while the CV is unchanged at 0.13. A pipeline reading raw
variance would have reported a crowd that was a gain step.
cards.explanation:
Coefficient of variation of CSI amplitude: the standard deviation over the
mean, computed on one subcarrier over a time window. It measures how much
the channel WOBBLES relative to how strong it is, as a dimensionless number
comparable between links and between captures.

In human terms first. A fifty-euro swing means one thing on a weekly food
shop and nothing at all on a house price, so a raw spread is only
interpretable next to a level. CV is the swing divided by the level, which
is why it can be compared at all.

Then there are two separate reasons to use it here, and they are worth
keeping apart because only one of them is principled.

The blunt reason: amplitude is relative to the receiver's automatic gain,
so absolute variance is not comparable between captures or receivers, and a
ratio is much closer to being so.

The principled reason: the derivation prescribes this exact normaliser.
Model the channel as a fixed component from things that never move — walls,
floor, shelves — plus a sum of moving phasors from the people. The fixed
component IS the mean amplitude. So dividing by the mean is dividing by the
static channel that the derivation says sets the scale, and the result is a
quantity about the movers alone.

This is the workhorse feature of the thesis. When the count relation is
described as sign-stable across every environment but platform-stratified
in scale, this is the quantity being described — and its sign-stability is
what makes presence detection transfer while absolute counting does not.

fields.meaning: standard deviation of amplitude on subcarrier k across the window
mean amplitude on that subcarrier — the static part of the channel
number of records in the window
wobble as a fraction of level — dimensionless, so comparable

figures.caption: Both curves sit on the same mean, and the occupied one wobbles more about it. CV is the size of that wobble expressed as a fraction of the level — which is the quantity that survives a gain change, because both numerator and denominator move together.

curves.label: quiet room: small wobble on a level
the mean the wobble is divided by

cards.question:
CV — define it for CSI, and say why dividing by the mean is principled
rather than convenient.
cards.reading:
On one subcarrier, take the standard deviation of amplitude over a time
window and divide it by the mean amplitude over the same window.
cards.title: Coefficient of variation

cards.back:
Cell occupancy: the number of bodies inside one spatial cell — a room, a
zone, a sensing region — at one moment. It is an integer, and it is the
quantity the whole system is trying to estimate.

Three things it is not, in increasing order of how easy they are to confuse
with it.

It is not a **building headcount**: occupancy is per cell, and a building
total cannot be disaggregated back into cells.
It is not a **device count**: a device count is what the reference channel
measures, and it is off by the device-to-person ratio.
It is not an **identifier count**: phones randomise their addresses, so one
phone can appear as several identifiers, which overcounts devices before
you even reach the harder question of devices versus people.
cards.example:
One lecture room at one instant, counted four ways: **28** bodies in the
room, **31** phones and laptops with a radio awake, **44** distinct
MAC addresses observed in the last minute, and **1** number the building
management system would report for the floor.

Only the first is N. The third is what a naive passive scan delivers, and
it is high by more than half — which is why the thesis treats identifier
counting as a biased instrument to be calibrated rather than as ground
truth. The specific figures here are illustrative of the ordering, not a
measurement: our own certified-empty sessions put every one of these at
zero, which is the one occupancy this deployment has established.

figures.caption: The four quantities a "count" can mean, and who produces each. The thesis estimates the first and measures the second; the gap between them is a latent to be identified, never a constant to be imported.
rows: passive BLE or WiFi activity scan
a sum over cells, not invertible

cards.front: N — what is it, and what are the three things it is NOT?
cards.title: Occupancy
cards.why:
Bodies, not radios. The thesis is careful about this because its reference
counts radios, and the device-to-person ratio is treated as a jointly
identified latent rather than an imported constant.

cards.back:
The occupancy at the variance–blockage crossover: below it, line-of-sight
blockage (falling mean amplitude) dominates; above it, multipath variance
(rising spread) dominates.

Two mechanisms, competing rather than adding. With a strong direct path a
body BLOCKS a large share of the arriving energy, so the mean drops. Once
the channel is already a diffuse mixture of comparable paths, an extra body
mostly STIRS the mixture, so the spread rises while the mean barely moves.
cards.example:
The practical form of this is which feature a pipeline should trust in
which room, and it is answerable by geometry before any data arrives.

A narrow corridor with the transmitter at one end and the receiver at the
other has one dominant path, so the first person to walk into it drops the
mean sharply — blockage, below the crossover. A furnished reading room with
shelving between the nodes has no dominant path at all, so the first person
changes the mean very little and the variability immediately: above the
crossover from the first occupant.

That is why the deployed pipeline keeps BOTH feature families rather than
picking the better one. The better one is a property of the room.

figures.caption: Illustrative shapes, not measured data. Blockage saturates fast — the first body takes most of the direct path and the second has less left to take. Variance keeps climbing. Where they cross is N*, and lowering the blockage curve, as 2.4 GHz does, moves the crossing to zero.

cards.front: N* — what crosses over, in which direction, and what decides where?
cards.title: The crossover
cards.why:
It is band-dependent. In the ray-traced study the channel is
variance-dominant from about zero occupants at 2.4 GHz, with a short
blockage-led regime at 5 GHz. These are simulation-derived and not yet
validated against measured CSI.

cards.back:
The recalibration interval: how long CSI-only inference stays inside a
tolerated error before the system must re-anchor. It is the RQ4
deliverable, and it is one half of an answer PAIR — the other half is the
error you agreed to absorb while waiting.
cards.example:
The everyday shape of this question is a bathroom scale. It reads correctly
today; in six months it is a kilogram out. The interval is not a property
of the scale alone — it is a property of the scale, the tolerance you accept
and how much the room's temperature moved.

What this deployment can already state is the drift mechanism the interval
will be built on. Over a twelve-hour baseline the per-node phase-drift
slope rank-ordered perfectly with mean die temperature — Spearman ρ of
−1.000 on five nodes, p = 0.0167. That is a strong monotone trend on a
small sample, and it is a lead rather than an established effect. It is
enough to say that T* has a thermal term; it is not enough to say what T*
is, and the thesis does not.

figures.caption: The SHAPE of the answer, with the axes labelled and the numbers deliberately absent. T* is where a rising error curve crosses a declared tolerance, so it cannot be quoted without ε — and this thesis has the protocol for measuring both and no measurement of either.

curves.label: error growing as the channel drifts

cards.front: T* — what is it, and what is its current status?
cards.title: The recalibration interval
cards.why:
Status matters as much as definition. (T*, ε) is DESIGNED AND BOUNDED, NOT
YET NUMBERED — it is the labelled result slot of the pre-registered drift
study, and the thesis says so rather than estimating it.

cards.back:
The tolerated accuracy degradation between calibrations — the other half of
the RQ4 answer pair (T*, ε). It is a DECLARED quantity, chosen by whoever
operates the building, not estimated from data.
cards.example:
Two buildings, same sensor, same drift, different ε — and therefore
different intervals from the same physics.

A lecture-hall scheduler that only needs to know whether a room is under
half full can accept ε of several persons, and will re-anchor rarely. A
ventilation controller sizing airflow per person accepts much less, and
pays for it in calibration visits. Neither is more correct; they are two
points on one frontier.

The measured version of that frontier is already in the thesis, and it is a
cost rather than a free lunch: the drift-triggered rule spends roughly half
the calibration budget of a fixed schedule, at a small accuracy cost, and
it FAILED an equivalence test against that schedule. So the honest claim is
the trade, not parity.

figures.caption: The same drift curve as the T* card, read the other way round: pick a tolerance on the horizontal axis and it tells you the interval. The shape is what the pre-registered study will measure; the numbers on the axes are placeholders for a result the thesis has not yet earned.

curves.label: the frontier: looser tolerance buys longer intervals

cards.front: ε — what is it, and why is T* meaningless without it?
cards.title: The tolerance
cards.why:
T* is meaningless alone. "Recalibrate every N hours" is only a policy once
you say what error you were willing to absorb in the meantime.

cards.example:
Here it carries a refutation condition, written before the data, which is
what makes it a hypothesis test rather than a diagnostic.

The uniform-material premise — that treating every wall as drywall is good
enough for synthetic CSI — is FALSIFIED if the CIR delay-spread
distributions for uniform-drywall geometry and material-tagged geometry
turn out statistically indistinguishable: **D below 0.05 across at least
200 transmitter–receiver pairs**.

Note the direction. A small D here refutes the value of the material
modelling, not the material modelling's correctness — if tagging every wall
with its real permittivity changes nothing measurable, the effort is not
buying anything. Declaring the threshold and the sample size in advance is
what stops that from becoming an argument after the fact.
cards.explanation:
The two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic. Both samples are turned into
cumulative distributions — for each value on the axis, what fraction of the
sample falls below it — and D is the biggest vertical gap between the two
curves anywhere.

Two properties make it useful. It assumes NOTHING about the shape of either
distribution, so it works on skewed, multimodal or heavy-tailed data where
a difference of means would mislead. And it is sensitive to any difference
in shape, not only to a shift in the middle: two samples with identical
means and different spreads have a large D.

Small D means the two samples could plausibly have come from the same
distribution. Large D means they could not. It is a distance, so it is
reported alongside a p-value rather than instead of one.

fields.meaning: the two empirical cumulative distributions being compared
the largest value over all x — the widest gap, not the average gap
one number between 0 and 1; 0 is identical, 1 is disjoint

figures.caption: Two cumulative curves; D is the widest vertical gap between them. Scrub the shift: at the first frame the curves lie on top of each other and D is near the refutation threshold, which is what "statistically indistinguishable" looks like as a picture.

cards.question:
D_KS — what does it measure, and what refutation condition does it carry
here?
cards.reading:
The largest vertical gap, anywhere along the axis, between two samples'
cumulative distribution functions.
cards.title: The KS statistic

cards.example:
The count-locus argument runs on exactly this asymmetry, with feature type
as the only thing that varies.

Static per-link amplitude scores strongly WITHIN one furnished room and
collapses across rooms, because what it learned was that room's multipath
map. Temporal-variance and Doppler features score lower in-room and
transfer, because what they learned was body dynamics.

One feature family, two scores, one honest conclusion: when the
environment changes, what breaks a trained model is the feature TYPE rather
than the radio that produced it.
cards.explanation:
The coefficient of determination: the share of the variance in the thing
you are predicting that your model actually accounts for. The denominator
is what you would suffer by always guessing the average, so R² compares the
model against the laziest possible competitor.

R² = 1 means the model reproduces every wiggle. R² = 0 means it does no
better than always guessing the mean. And it can go **negative** on
held-out data, which is not a bug and not a numerical error: it means the
model's predictions are further from the truth than a flat line would have
been.

That negative regime is the one that matters here, because it is what a
fingerprint feature does when you move it to another room. It has not
merely lost accuracy; it is now actively misleading, mapping this room's
multipath pattern onto counts that belonged to a different room.

Read it with one caution the statistics corpus insists on: R² measured on
the data a model was fitted to always rises when you add parameters, so it
is only informative on held-out data. In-sample R² is a description, not an
evaluation.

fields.meaning: the truth for observation i — here, the real occupancy
what the model predicted
the mean of the truth — the do-nothing baseline
1 is perfect, 0 is no better than the mean, negative is worse

figures.caption: Illustrative of the mechanism the thesis measures, not measured values. The dashed line is not the floor: a model can score below it, and a per-room amplitude map moved to another room does exactly that.

curves.label: a fingerprint feature: strong, then worse than nothing
a kinematic feature: degrades and survives

markers.label: below this the model is worse than the mean

figures.x_label: how far the model is out of its training domain

cards.question:
R² — what does it actually measure, and what does a NEGATIVE value on
held-out data mean?
cards.reading:
One minus the model's squared error divided by the squared error of always
guessing the average.
cards.title: R-squared

cards.back:
An explicit, defeasible claim stated TOGETHER WITH the condition under
which it would be considered refuted, and maintained as a
version-controlled note revised as evidence accumulates.

Three parts, all required. The **claim**. The **refutation condition**,
written before the data arrive, in numbers. And the **record** — a note
whose history shows what was believed when, so a claim cannot quietly
become weaker or stronger between drafts.
cards.example:
The continuity prior is the worked example, and it is a real one.

The claim was that a mass-conservation penalty would improve indoor
density estimation. The refutation condition was declared first: if
swapping the physics term for a constant, or for an ANTI-physical version,
does not change the result, the term is not acting as physics.

It was run and it fired. Matched, constant and anti-physical closures
landed on the same error, and plain smoothing with no conservation content
beat every variant. The hypothesis was retired, and it is on the record
with its evidence rather than deleted from the draft — which is what makes
the surviving hypotheses believable.

figures.caption: An ordinary hypothesis and a living one, side by side. The difference is not rigour in the abstract — it is that the second one can be lost.
rows: the note's history shows what changed

cards.front:
Define "living hypothesis" as this thesis uses it. What makes it different
from an ordinary research hypothesis?
cards.title: Living hypothesis
cards.why:
The refutation condition is written BEFORE the data arrive, which is what
keeps the record honest in a field where claims are hardware-gated. The
proof that it works is on the record: one hypothesis in this programme has
already fired its refutation condition and been retired.

choices: It is inconsistent — a chosen hypothesis must be at least supported.
The thesis has committed to pursuing it, but the evidence it has earned so far is only plausible.
It was chosen by the supervisor rather than by the evidence.
It is plausible enough to publish but not chosen for the defense.
cards.example:
Read the pair as a project-management fact and an epistemic fact, which is
what they are.

"Chosen" says: fleet time, hardware and chapter space are being spent on
this. "Plausible" says: if you asked today whether it is true, the answer is
a mechanism and a partial result, not a demonstration. A grant reviewer
cares about the first. A committee cares about the second. Collapsing them
into one word would let a well-funded claim look well-supported.

The pair also explains why the honest headline is "periodic recalibration
is DESIGNED AND BOUNDED, not yet numbered" rather than a number.
cards.explanation:
The two axes are deliberately orthogonal. Lifecycle state records the
decision history — candidate, chosen, deferred, refuted, superseded.
Evidence strength records what the claim has EARNED — speculative,
plausible, supported, strong. Periodic recalibration, the headline
deployment claim, sits at exactly chosen/plausible: committed to, and not
yet carrying the evidence that would make it strong. Reporting that pair
honestly is the point of having two axes.

figures.caption: The two axes and their values. Any state can pair with any strength — that is what orthogonal means here, and refuted/strong is the combination a documented negative occupies.

cards.question: A hypothesis is marked "chosen" and "plausible". What does that pair mean?
cards.title: Lifecycle state versus evidence strength

cards.back:
A labelled observation in a NEW environment — a device-derived count the
operator is entitled to collect, paired with a CSI window. The headline
cross-environment result uses two per held-out environment.

Two properties make it an anchor rather than just a training sample. It
comes from the TARGET environment, so it carries that room's scale. And it
is one the operator may legitimately obtain — which is a claim about
entitlement, not only about availability.
cards.example:
Concretely, in a building you have just walked into: stand in the room,
count the people once, and record the CSI window alongside that count.
Do it twice. That is the entire cost of the headline calibration result,
and it is the reason the result is deployable rather than only true.

Compare the alternatives that lost. Riemannian covariance transport, run
under a declared kill line, recovered only a small share of the
cross-environment gap. A three-anchor affine rescale actively HURT,
inflating error more than twofold. Two labelled points beat all of it —
and the honest reading is not that the clever methods are bad, but that a
little bit of target-domain truth is worth a great deal of machinery.

figures.caption: What an anchor is and where it comes from. The shared link is fitted on every environment; the two anchors supply the new room's scale and nothing else. Everything below the dashed line is unlabelled.

cards.front:
What is an "anchor" in the calibration spine, and how many does the
headline result use?
cards.title: Anchor
cards.why:
Two is the surprise. Four mathematically independent LABEL-FREE
alternatives were run under pre-registered kill lines and every one lost
to those two anchors, for a reason domain-adaptation theory names in
advance.

choices: Restores the model to its original factory calibration.
Re-identifies the drifted CSI-to-count map by a local re-fit on trustworthy labelled anchors.
Applies a published device-to-person conversion factor to the current estimate.
Retrains the whole model from scratch on freshly collected labelled CSI.
cards.example:
A kitchen scale is the honest analogy for all four options, and it
separates them cleanly.

**Reset** is pressing tare with the bowl still on: it removes an offset you
may not have had, and does nothing about a slope that has changed.
**Re-fit** is putting a known 500 g weight on and correcting the reading:
two known points and the instrument is trustworthy again.
**Retrain** is buying a new scale, which is what a full re-collection of
labelled CSI amounts to in a deployed building.
**Importing a factor** is reading someone else's calibration certificate
for a different scale and applying it to yours.

Only the second is cheap AND correct, and it is the only one that needs
something the operator can actually get: a couple of labelled counts.
cards.explanation:
Recalibration is a local RE-FIT, not a reset and not a full retrain, and
the distinction is measured rather than stylistic: on the material-drift
sweep, re-identification recovered most of the count-MAE penalty while
reset-only recovered almost none. It is also not a cheap rescale — in one
reduction a three-anchor affine rescale actively HURT, inflating error
more than twofold. And it is emphatically not option three: importing a
literature conversion factor is the practice the device–person
identification hypothesis exists to replace.

figures.caption: Four things people mean by "recalibrate", what each costs, and what each recovered where the thesis measured it.
rows: worse than nothing in one reduction — error more than doubled

cards.question: What does recalibration DO in this architecture?
cards.title: Recalibration

cards.back:
A certified-empty window is one where the space is verified unoccupied AND
a live-receiver control proves the measurement was being taken.

Both halves are needed, and the second is the one people forget. A zero
from a working receiver in an empty room is a measurement. A zero from a
dead receive path is a fault. They are the same number.
cards.example:
The control is the infrastructure traffic, and it is the part of the design
worth stealing.

Access points, printers and building equipment transmit whether or not
anybody is present. So in every certified-empty hour the capture shows
**infrastructure addresses present and client addresses at exactly zero**.
The first proves the receiver was listening; the second is the measurement.
Over a thousand minutes of that, the floor of the device-activity channel
is a fact rather than an assumption.

The fault class this defends against is real and was observed on this
fleet: silent deafness, where every service reports healthy, the sidecar
metadata is written, and zero CSI records arrive. Without a positive
control that session would have been a thousand minutes of "empty room".

figures.caption: Why a zero needs a witness. The two rows are indistinguishable in the data unless something is known to be transmitting.
rows: a fault: nothing is being heard

cards.front:
What makes a room "certified empty" rather than just empty, and why does
the distinction carry a result?
cards.title: Certified empty
cards.why:
Without the control, a zero client count is indistinguishable from a dead
receive path. With it, the zero is a measurement: over a thousand minutes
of certified-empty observation the distinct client-address count is zero,
while infrastructure addresses were captured in every certified-empty
hour. That is what makes the device-activity channel's floor interpretable
— and it is a wasting asset that disappears when the semester begins.

cards.back:
That they are quantities OF THE SENSING INSTRUMENT, on the same footing as
the count itself — not deployment plumbing to be reported once and set
aside.

A measurand is something the instrument is understood to measure, with a
stated uncertainty, whose value is part of every result. Calling delivery a
measurand commits the thesis to reporting it per analysis window, next to
the occupancy estimate, for ever.
cards.example:
Two receivers, one transmitter, one channel, one moment — and an
**11.6-point difference in delivered fraction** between them. A study with
one monitor would have recorded whichever of those two numbers its monitor
happened to be, and called it the delivery rate.

The census that goes with it is the same lesson at record level: across
four nodes on 2026-08-23, **98.4% of commanded frames were delivered**,
and **15–16% of the delivered records carried an all-zero I/Q matrix** —
a valid header, the right length, a plausible RSSI, and no measurement
inside. So the useful yield is about **83%**, not 98.4%. Quoting delivery
without the empty-record count overstates the data by fifteen points.

figures.caption: The three instrument measurands, what each is, and what a single-monitor study can say about it. The last column is the argument.
rows: fraction of commanded frames that produced a record
one number, unaware it is one of several
**records with a valid header and no I/Q**
how busy the medium was while measuring

cards.front:
The thesis calls delivery, loss and channel occupancy "measurands". What
is the claim inside that word?
cards.title: Measurand
cards.why:
The claim has teeth because a single monitor cannot see them. It takes a
synchronous multi-receiver array to observe an 11.6-point delivery spread
between receivers hearing the same transmitter on the same channel, and
no corpus paper reports the delivered fraction of a commanded probe.

cards.back:
**Fingerprint** features — per-link absolute CSI amplitude maps, per-link
BLE-RSSI vectors — encode the spatial multipath MAP of one furnished room.
**Kinematic** features — multipath-change rate, temporal amplitude
variance, fading statistics — encode body DYNAMICS.

The test that separates them is a question, not a formula: if you moved
this feature to another room, would its VALUES still mean the same thing? A
fingerprint's values are indexed to a geometry. A kinematic's values are
indexed to motion, which is the same everywhere.
cards.example:
Face recognition against gait recognition, which is the same distinction in
a domain everyone can picture.

A face template is a fingerprint: extremely accurate on the person it was
built for, and worthless transferred to anybody else. A gait descriptor —
cadence, stride length, sway — is kinematic: less sharp, and it means the
same thing about a person it has never seen.

In our data the same split lands on the same modality twice. Per-link BLE
RSSI vectors and per-link CSI amplitude maps are both fingerprints and both
break on a move. CSI temporal variance and BLE arrival-rate dynamics are
both kinematic and both survive it. Sorting the literature by radio
produces a contradiction; sorting it by feature type dissolves one.

figures.caption: The sort that matters. Note that both columns contain both radios — which is the finding, since the field usually sorts by radio.
rows: the multipath map of one room

cards.front:
Define a fingerprint feature and a kinematic feature, and state what each
encodes.
cards.title: Fingerprint versus kinematic
cards.why:
The split is the point: when the environment changes, what breaks a
trained model is the feature TYPE, not the RF modality. That reconciles
several apparently conflicting reports of CSI robustness once features are
sorted by type rather than by the radio that produced them.

choices: Environment-level shift is larger; encoding-level shift is a second-order correction.
Environment-level shift is additive to the target signal and leaves its encoding intact; encoding-level shift changes how the event is written into the channel at all.
Environment-level shift affects amplitude and encoding-level shift affects phase.
Environment-level shift happens over time; encoding-level shift happens in space.
cards.example:
Photography, and the analogy is tight enough to be useful.

Moving the furniture in a room is environment-level: the photograph changes
and the CAMERA still turns light into pixels the same way. Swapping to a
different sensor with a different colour response is encoding-level: every
photograph you ever took with the first camera now maps onto different
numbers, and no amount of rearranging furniture will fix that.

The field's own benchmarks show the second one biting. A published CSI
dataset that recorded the same activities behind two different router
brands found the hardware change deserved attention in its own right, and a
reproducibility protocol paper puts it plainly: models trained on one
chipset degrade severely on another, partly because vendors lay out their
subcarriers differently. That is not a room changing. That is the encoder
changing.
cards.explanation:
Room geometry, furniture and other scatterers are ADDITIVE to the target
signal — models transfer across them reliably. Hardware, receiver
placement and carrier channel change the MAPPING itself, and models
degrade substantially across those. The distinction matters twice over.
It explains why hardware shift dominates layout shift in this thesis's own
data, and it sharpens the dual-use question: the axis on which
recalibration would most help an unauthorised observer is the axis on
which that observer cannot obtain anchors.

figures.caption: Two axes, two prognoses. The right-hand column is why calibration in this thesis is per DEVICE and not merely per room.

cards.question: What separates ENVIRONMENT-level shift from ENCODING-level shift?
cards.title: Two kinds of shift

cards.back:
The output of a CSI occupancy estimator is a predictive DISTRIBUTION over
counts, P(N = k), with operational bands obtained by marginalisation at
query time. It replaces a point count with MAE as the figure of merit.

Marginalisation at query time is the load-bearing clause. The model reports
a distribution; the question "is this room more than half full?" is
answered by summing that distribution over the relevant counts WHEN THE
QUESTION IS ASKED. Band edges are therefore a query-time choice, not a
training-time commitment.
cards.example:
A ventilation controller and a fire marshal ask the same sensor two
different questions on the same second.

Ventilation wants the expected number, to size airflow. The marshal wants
P(N > 50), because that is the threshold in the regulation. From one
predictive distribution both are a summation. From one point estimate of
"34 people" the second question has no answer at all — 34 is either under
50 or it is not, with no statement of how sure.

And the honest part: the same distribution also answers "which band" for a
band the operator invents next year, without retraining, because the bands
were never baked in.

figures.caption: Illustrative. Both distributions have the same mean, so a point contract reports the same "34" for both, and average error cannot separate them. Only the wide one admits that P(N > 50) is not negligible — which is the whole difference between the two contracts under environment shift.

curves.label: out of domain: the SAME mean, wider

cards.front: What is the thesis's output contract, and what does it replace?
cards.title: The output contract
cards.why:
Two reasons, both measured. The count mapping does not transfer cold
across environments, so a point estimand is a thin headline. And the
question a building asks is almost never "how many" but "which band, and
how sure".

choices: It would be computationally more expensive.
It recovers most of the calibration benefit but none of the shift-robustness, because a globally fixed width cannot widen specifically where the data is unfamiliar.
It is not conformally valid.
It would require labelled data in the target environment.
cards.example:
A weather forecast that says "±3 °C" on every single day, in every season,
in every location. It is not lying about its average performance. It is
simply unable to tell you that today is a day it does not understand.

That is exactly the failure mode measured here. A fixed-width band is
correctly sized ON AVERAGE and wrong where it matters — in the unfamiliar
room, at the unfamiliar occupancy — because the width was never allowed to
depend on the input.
cards.explanation:
The cheaper alternative was run and it fails in a diagnostic way. Its
width is set by a global residual variance, so it cannot widen where the
model is out of its depth. The benefit of the full distribution comes from
the model being able to express WHERE it is uncertain, not merely how much
on average. The same section also rules out the other cheap option — a
classifier trained directly on fixed bands measured equally accurate to
within a rounding error, but it makes band edges a training-time
commitment instead of a query-time choice.

figures.caption: Illustrative of the mechanism. The dashed line is right on average and wrong everywhere in particular: too wide where the model is confident, far too narrow where it is lost. Averaged error cannot see the difference, which is why the thesis scores contracts on calibration too.

curves.label: fixed width from a global residual

cards.question:
Why not simply attach the residual standard deviation to the existing
point model instead of predicting a full distribution?
cards.title: Why not just attach an error bar

cards.back:
Distribution-free prediction intervals with approximately nominal
coverage — an interval you can promise contains the truth 90% of the time,
without assuming anything about the shape of the error distribution.

The machinery is one idea: score the model's errors on a held-out
calibration set, take the quantile of those scores at the level you want,
and use it as the interval width. In-environment split conformal is valid
at usable width. But zero-shot transfer collapses where exchangeability
does, and anchoring on two calibration points repairs that collapse almost
completely.
cards.example:
Exchangeability is the assumption, so it is worth seeing it break.

Take a hundred labelled windows from THIS room, score the model's errors on
them, and the 90th percentile of those errors is a width that will cover
about 90% of future windows from this room. That is the guarantee, and it
holds with no distributional assumption whatsoever.

Now move to a different building. The new room's errors are not drawn from
the same pool as the calibration room's, so the quantile you computed is
the wrong quantile, and coverage falls below nominal — silently, because
nothing in the arithmetic notices. Two labelled anchors from the new room
are enough to re-point it, which is the same two anchors the calibration
spine already needs.

figures.caption: Illustrative of the mechanism the thesis reports. More calibration data fixes the first curve and does nothing for the second: a bigger sample from the wrong distribution is still the wrong distribution, which is what "collapses where exchangeability does" means.

cards.front: What does the conformal wrapper add, and what is its honest limitation?
cards.title: Conformal prediction
cards.why:
The limitation is stated, not buried: per-environment validity is NOT
uniform at commodity calibration-set sizes, and exact conditional coverage
is provably unattainable at finite sample. So the citable claim is a
mechanism result plus a finite-sample limitation, never a uniform
guarantee.

cards.back:
One model with a SHARED crowd-to-signal link and PER-ENVIRONMENT
parameters, nested under a WiFi-card group. Neither pooling everything
(which ignores real per-site scale differences) nor fitting each site
alone (which throws away the shared mechanism).

The mechanism has a name and a formula: shrinkage. Each site's estimate is
pulled towards the population mean by an amount that depends on how much
data that site has. A site with two observations is pulled almost all the
way; a site with two hundred barely moves.
cards.example:
A chain of twenty shops estimating tomorrow's takings, which is the
standard example because the arithmetic is identical.

Pool everything and every shop gets the chain average, which is wrong for
the airport branch. Fit each shop alone and the one that opened last week
gets an estimate built from four days of noise. Partial pooling gives the
new shop mostly the chain average and the established one mostly its own
history — automatically, with the weight set by the data volume rather than
by taste.

Here the shops are environments, the takings are the signal-to-count scale,
and the new shop with four days of data is a building you have just walked
into with two anchors in hand. The 42% recovery figure is what that
arithmetic predicts, which is why it is a mechanism rather than a
coincidence.

figures.caption: The shape of the shrinkage argument. The first anchors buy the most, which is why two is a defensible operating point and twenty would be hard to justify. Full pooling cannot use an anchor at all; no pooling cannot use only two.

curves.label: no pooling: needs its own campaign
full pooling: flat, whatever you collect

figures.x_label: anchors available in the new environment
figures.y_label: share of the transfer gap recovered

cards.front: What does "partial pooling" mean here, and what does it buy?
cards.title: Partial pooling
cards.why:
It explains the measured two-anchor recovery as empirical-Bayes shrinkage
toward the population prior, with a closed-form recovery-versus-anchors
curve — turning "we saw 42 per cent recovery" into "the model says two
anchors must recover about this much, and they do."

cards.example:
Fire extinguishers on an office floor, which is submodular for the same
reason.

The first one covers a large area of what was previously unprotected. The
fourth, placed in a corner already within reach of two others, adds very
little. Nobody solves an integer program for extinguisher placement — they
place them greedily, and the theorem says that habit is within a third of
optimal.

In our own setting the same shape appeared with a sting: room adjacency
looked like it should predict which floors are easy to cover, and it did
not. What drove recoverability was receiver DENSITY and placement — the two
things the greedy objective is actually about.
cards.explanation:
Two properties, both about sets rather than about numbers.
**Monotone**: adding a sensor never reduces coverage. **Submodular**: the
marginal gain of adding one shrinks as the set grows — formally, adding to
a subset helps at least as much as adding to a superset.

What you get for it is a theorem. Greedy placement — repeatedly add the
single sensor that helps most right now — carries the Nemhauser–Wolsey–
Fisher guarantee of reaching at least 1 − 1/e, about 63%, of the optimum.
That converts an intractable combinatorial search into a loop you can run,
with a bound you can state.

It also exposes a trade-off that is easy to miss. Covering the paths people
TAKE and concentrating sensing on the busy HUB are different submodular
objectives, so coverage-optimal and counting-optimal placements differ and
neither dominates. Choosing between them is a design decision, and the
guarantee applies to whichever you chose — it does not tell you which to
want.

fields.meaning: coverage achieved by a set of sensor positions
a smaller placement set inside a larger one
about 0.632 — the Nemhauser–Wolsey–Fisher guarantee
the optimal placement, which nobody computes

figures.caption: Diminishing returns IS submodularity, drawn. Each sensor adds less than the one before, and that single property is what licenses the guarantee — no optimisation required, and a bound you can quote.

cards.latex: f(A \cup \{s\}) - f(A) \;\geq\; f(B \cup \{s\}) - f(B) \quad \text{for } A \subseteq B, \qquad f(A_{\mathrm{greedy}}) \geq \left(1 - \tfrac{1}{e}\right) f(A^{*})
cards.question:
What does it mean that sensor placement is monotone submodular, and what
do you get for it?
cards.reading:
Adding a sensor to a smaller set helps at least as much as adding it to a
bigger set — and greedy therefore reaches at least sixty-three per cent of
the best possible.
cards.title: Submodular

cards.example:
Our own numbers, one window at a time.

A 2 × 2 frame on a 20 MHz HE channel gives p = 4 × 242 = **968**
dimensions. At the measured 608 Hz, a **one-second** window gives n = 608,
so γ ≈ 1.6 and the noise edge sits near 5.1 σ² — a high bar. A
**ten-second** window gives n = 6080, γ ≈ 0.16, and the edge falls to about
1.9 σ². Same room, same people, and the detectable occupancy changed
because the window changed.

This is also the tone-count trap in its exact form: moving to 996 tones
quadruples p, so a result obtained on 56 subcarriers is not a result on 996
unless n moved too.
cards.explanation:
p is antenna × subcarrier dimensions, n is snapshots in the window, and γ
is the aspect ratio of the sample covariance.

It sets the detection edge. With pure noise, the sample covariance's
eigenvalues do not sit at σ² — they spread into a bulk whose upper edge is
σ²(1 + √γ)². An occupant becomes spectrally visible only once its
eigenvalue detaches from that bulk, which is a threshold fixed by the
measurement geometry rather than by the room.

Two consequences follow, and both are about design rather than analysis.
**Saturation** is the regime in which added occupants fall below that edge —
so a saturation knee is a property of p and n, not a constant of the space.
And **short windows make p ≈ n**, so the covariance is ill-conditioned and
needs shrinkage before any eigenvalue is trustworthy.

fields.meaning: dimensions — antenna × subcarrier, so 968 on a 2×2 242-tone frame
snapshots in the window — records, so 608 per second here
the aspect ratio of the sample covariance matrix
the upper edge of the noise bulk — the detection threshold

figures.caption: The detection edge as a function of measurement geometry alone. An occupant is spectrally visible only once its eigenvalue clears this line, and the line rises with γ — so a short window raises the bar without anything in the room changing.

markers.label: γ = 1 — as many dimensions as snapshots

figures.y_label: noise-bulk upper edge, in units of σ²

cards.question: γ = p/n — name p, name n, and say what γ decides.
cards.reading:
The aspect ratio is dimensions over snapshots, and the noise eigenvalues
reach up to sigma squared times one plus the root of gamma, squared.
cards.title: The aspect ratio

cards.example:
A lecture room, and the same room an hour later, with the same sensor.

During the lecture: 30 students, most with a phone awake and a laptop on
the desk, r·p above one — the device count exceeds the headcount and a
naive conversion overstates the crowd. During the exam: 30 students, phones
in bags with the radios asleep, r·p well below one — the same conversion
now understates it.

Nothing about the room, the sensor or the people changed. What changed was
a behaviour, and it moved the conversion factor in both directions within
an hour. That is why the thesis treats r·p as a jointly identified latent
rather than a constant to be imported from a citation.
cards.explanation:
Detection rate times device-carriage penetration — the single scalar that
converts a device count into a headcount.

It is a sufficient statistic because the count error depends on the
PRODUCT, and no measurement of a device count can separate the factors.
Halve the detection rate and double the carriage and the observable is
unchanged. So a study that reports "we assumed 1.2 devices per person"
without a detection rate has reported half of a quantity.

Which is why the participant protocol measures the product by
construction: Phase I sets penetration to one so the product is the
detection rate, and Phase II makes penetration a covariate. An anchor that
miscounts devices is worse than no anchor, because a wrong anchor is
applied with confidence.

fields.meaning: devices observed — what the reference channel measures
detection rate — the share of present devices actually seen
penetration — devices carried per person
the headcount being estimated

figures.caption: Only the PRODUCT appears on the axis, because only the product can be identified from a device count. Assuming unity when the truth is 0.6 undercounts by forty per cent; assuming unity when the truth is 1.4 overcounts by the same kind of margin.

curves.label: error if you assume r·p = 1 and it is not

cards.question:
What is r·p, and why does the thesis insist it is a sufficient statistic
rather than two numbers?
cards.reading:
The device count is detection rate times carriage penetration times the
number of people, so converting back divides by the product of the two.
cards.title: The device-to-person ratio

cards.back:
A hypothesis that was specified, tested under pre-registered margins, and
refuted — kept on the record with its reproducible evidence rather than
deleted from the draft.

Three conditions, all of them needed for the word to apply. The claim was
stated in advance. The margin that would refute it was stated in advance.
And the evidence is reproducible, so the retirement can be checked rather
than believed.
cards.example:
Three of them are on the record, and they cost the thesis three different
things.

The **continuity prior** was refuted by an ablation in which anti-physical
and constant closures performed identically to the correct one. That
retired a tier of the architecture.
The **certified-empty false-trigger constraint** came out of running a
purely statistical drift trigger over twelve certified-empty hours: it
fired on a third of the streams at a detected shift of a few thousandths of
a decibel. Statistically real, physically meaningless — so the deployed
trigger gained a magnitude gate.
The **delay-spread band contrast** died under re-reduction, and with it
every multipath-richness argument that narrow-bandwidth hardware could have
carried.

Each one is now a design somebody else does not have to spend a year on.

figures.caption: The three, with what refuted each and what the thesis changed as a result. A negative with no consequence is not a contribution; these each moved something.
rows: a tier of the architecture retired
fired on a third of certified-empty streams

cards.front:
What is a "documented negative" in this thesis, and why is it counted as a
contribution?
cards.title: Documented negative
cards.why:
Because each one retires a design the field would otherwise keep
proposing. The continuity prior is attractive enough that it WILL be
proposed again, so the evidence that retires it has to remain exactly
reproducible.

cards.back:
**Silent deafness** — every service green, sidecar metadata written, zero
CSI records, and the only symptom a frozen kernel receive counter.
And a **transient single-node delivery collapse** that co-located
receivers on the same channel do not share.

Both are dangerous for the same reason: their signature in the data is
indistinguishable from the thing being measured. A receiver that hears
nothing looks exactly like a room with nobody in it.
cards.example:
The arithmetic of the gate grain, which is the actionable part.

Take a thirty-minute session with a ninety-second dead hole in the middle.
At session grain the delivery figure is about 95% — comfortably above any
reasonable threshold, so the session passes and the hole travels downstream.
At one-minute grain, one window reads 0% and is dropped, the neighbours are
partially degraded, and the surviving windows are all real measurements.

Same data, same threshold, two different corpora — and only the second one
can be read as occupancy. That is why the gate is specified at the window
grain rather than tightened at the session grain.

figures.caption: The two fault classes and what distinguishes each from a genuine empty room. Note that in both cases the SERVICE is healthy, which is why service health is not the witness.
columns: What proves it is a fault
rows: one node's delivery drops for a minute
co-located nodes on the same channel did not

cards.front:
Name the two receiver fault classes the instrument characterisation found,
and say why they are dangerous.
cards.title: Silent deafness
cards.why:
Both are FALSE-POSITIVE GENERATORS for a counting study, and both argue
that delivery gates belong at the analysis-window grain: a session
containing a ninety-second hole passes a session-grain gate.

cards.back:
A **scalar** is one number. A **vector** is an ordered n-tuple of numbers —
a list where the position carries meaning. A **matrix** is an n-by-m
rectangular array, so each element needs TWO indices to name it. Formally:
a vector lives in ℝⁿ, a matrix in ℝⁿˣᵐ, and an element of a matrix A is
written a(i,j) with i counting rows and j counting columns.

What decides which you get is how many independent ways the instrument can
be asked the same question. One power reading per frame: a scalar. One
reading per subcarrier: a vector, indexed by frequency. One reading per
subcarrier AND per antenna pair: a matrix, indexed by both.

Two operations are worth having cold, because the whole thesis leans on
them. The **inner product** of two vectors is the sum of their
element-by-element products — one number, which is why it can measure
similarity. The **norm** is the square root of a vector's inner product
with itself — its length.
cards.example:
One CSI record from our own hardware, unpacked into the three shapes.

RSSI for that frame: **a scalar**, one number, about −45 dBm. Amplitude
across the tone grid of a 20 MHz HE frame: **a vector** of 242 numbers.
The same frame across the node's two receive and two transmit chains:
**a 2 × 2 matrix per tone** — so 242 matrices, or equivalently a
242 × 2 × 2 block of complex numbers per frame.

The scalar is what RSSI-based counting works with. The vector is what most
published CSI work uses. The matrix is what our nodes actually deliver.

figures.caption: The same measurement at three shapes. Each step adds an index, and each index is a question the previous shape could not be asked.
House notation, so a symbol's shape is readable without context. It follows the convention of the vault's statistics corpus.

cards.front:
Scalar, vector, matrix — say what each one IS, and what decides which of
them a measurement gives you.
cards.title: Scalar, vector, matrix
cards.why:
Everyday version. Your electricity bill is a scalar: one number for the
month. The half-hourly meter reading is a vector: forty-eight numbers whose
ORDER is the whole point, because 3 a.m. and 6 p.m. mean different things.
A year of half-hourly readings is a matrix, and now you can ask a question
neither of the others can answer — is this Tuesday like last Tuesday.

cards.back:
In this thesis a **tensor** means exactly one thing: an array with more
than two indices. A vector has one, a matrix has two, a tensor has three
or more, and the number of indices is called its ORDER. Nothing about
curvature or physics is intended — the word is being used the way the
machine-learning literature uses it, as a named box of numbers with named
axes.

A CSI capture is the standard example, and the CSI literature builds it the
same way we do: one CSI data point is a complex matrix of size
W × N — W subcarriers by N receive chains — and stacking T consecutive
data points along time gives an order-3 tensor of size T × W × N.

The axes are not interchangeable, and that is the whole reason to name
them. Averaging along TIME gives you the room. Averaging along
SUBCARRIER destroys the frequency selectivity that made CSI worth having.
Averaging along ANTENNA throws away the viewpoints.
cards.example:
A one-minute capture from node monad05 at the measured 608 Hz on a 20 MHz
HE channel, laid out as the tensor the loader actually returns:

- time: about **36 000** records
- subcarrier: **242** tones on the used-tone grid
- antenna: **2 × 2** transmit-receive pairs

That is roughly 36 000 × 242 × 4 complex numbers for one minute on ONE
node. Nine receivers for an hour is where the archive's size comes from,
and it is why every reduction states which axis it collapsed first.

figures.caption: The axes of a capture tensor, and what each one is for. A reduction that does not say which axis it collapsed has not described itself.
rows: the static room — the average channel
**RSSI — the thing CSI exists to improve on**
one view of the room instead of four

figures.caption: One frame is a matrix of tones by antennas. Time stacks those frames into an order-3 tensor, and the node axis stacks those into the array this fleet actually is.

cards.front:
Tensor — what is it here, what are its axes, and why does the word appear
at all in a counting thesis?
cards.title: Tensor
cards.why:
Everyday version: a colour photograph. Height, width, and three colour
channels — an order-3 tensor. Nobody would average the red channel into the
blue one to "simplify" it, and for the same reason nobody should average a
CSI tensor across its tone axis and call the result CSI.

cards.example:
Take a tone measured as a = 0.30, b = −0.40 in the receiver's units. Then
|H| = √(0.09 + 0.16) = **0.50** and φ = arctan(−0.40 / 0.30) ≈ **−0.93 rad**,
about −53°.

Now the part that matters. Re-run the same capture a second later and the
0.50 is still about 0.50, while the −53° may be anywhere at all, because
the two radios' crystals have drifted in the meantime. The magnitude
survived the second; the angle did not. That is not a defect of our
hardware — it is why the CSI-ratio trick, which divides one antenna by
another on the same radio, exists at all.
cards.explanation:
A radio wave arriving at an antenna has two properties, not one: how big it
is and where in its cycle it is. A single real number cannot hold both, so
the receiver reports a complex number, and the two halves are exactly those
two properties.

The everyday version is a clock hand — a **phasor**. Its LENGTH is the
amplitude and its ANGLE is the phase. Two waves arriving together add like
two hands added tip to tail: pointing the same way they make a longer hand,
pointing opposite ways they cancel. That single picture is the whole of
multipath, and it is why a room full of reflections has deep nulls in it.

Which brings the practical asymmetry this thesis lives with. Amplitude is
usable nearly raw, and needs only mean-scaling because it is relative to
the receiver's automatic gain. Phase is contaminated on every single packet
by oscillator and timing offsets that are as large as the effect being
measured, so it must be repaired before it means anything. Same complex
number, two very different levels of trust.

fields.meaning: real and imaginary parts — what the receiver's two mixers actually deliver
magnitude, or amplitude — how much of the signal survived
phase, or angle — WHERE in its cycle the wave arrived
the square root of minus one; engineers write j, mathematicians i

figures.caption: Scrub the phase. The wave slides while the amplitude never moves — which is why amplitude and phase are two independent measurements of the same arriving wave, and why one of them can be usable while the other is not.

cards.question:
A CSI value is a COMPLEX number. What are its two halves, and what does
each one mean physically?
cards.reading:
One complex number, written two ways: as a real and an imaginary part, or
as a magnitude and an angle. The two forms hold the same information.
cards.title: Complex number and phasor

cards.back:
A tuple (states, alphabet/events, transition function, initial state,
accepting/final states); behaviour = allowed event-driven state
evolution. Used as the agent-behaviour layer of the IP-107 agenda engine
(persona FSMs with weighted transitions, dwell states, and exit
semantics) driving the pedestrian simulator.
cards.front:
Define a finite-state machine and name where the thesis toolchain uses
them.
cards.title: FSM

cards.back:
A bipartite graph of places (hold tokens) and transitions. A transition
is enabled when every input place holds the required tokens; firing
consumes them and produces tokens in output places. Natural for
concurrency: independence, synchronisation, and resource contention are
structural.
cards.front: What is a Petri net and what is the firing rule?
cards.title: Petri nets

cards.back:
Tokens carry typed data ("colours") and transitions have guards/
expressions over them — folding many identical subnets into one
parameterised net. Used in the Hermod systems paper (Konkoly thesis →
IEEE Systems Journal) to model the message-delivery pipeline.
cards.front:
What do Coloured Petri Nets add over plain Petri nets, and where did you
use them?
cards.title: Coloured Petri nets

cards.back:
Safety: "nothing bad ever happens" — violated by a finite trace (never
two agents in one seat). Liveness: "something good eventually happens" —
only violated in the infinite limit (every queued message is eventually
delivered). Model checkers treat them differently (finite counterexample
vs lasso).
cards.front: Safety vs liveness properties — definitions and one-line examples.
cards.title: Safety vs liveness

cards.back:
Exhaustive exploration of a system's state space to decide whether a
temporal-logic property holds, yielding a counterexample trace on
failure. Limitation: state-space explosion — the product of component
states grows exponentially, so abstraction/reduction is the whole game.
cards.front: What is model checking, and what is its fundamental limitation?
cards.title: Model checking

choices: Every request is eventually granted
Some request is eventually granted
Requests and grants alternate strictly
A grant can only follow a request immediately
cards.explanation:
G = always (globally), F = eventually (finally): at every point, if
request holds then at some later point grant holds — the canonical
response/liveness pattern.
cards.question: In LTL, what does G(request → F grant) express?
cards.title: Temporal logic

cards.back:
Verification: did we build the model right (does the implementation meet
its spec — e.g. sim_scenario_validate's strict schema + floor cross-ref
before any run). Validation: did we build the right model (does the sim
correspond to reality — e.g. the OPERAnet sim-to-real check). A verified
simulator can still be an invalid model of the world.
cards.front:
Verification vs validation — and how the distinction maps onto the
simulation platform.
cards.title: Verification vs validation

cards.back:
Reproducibility: identical inputs must yield identical artefacts or
results can't be audited or cached. Examples: the deck compiler and
contribution-map are LLM-free with content-hash versions; workflow
scripts ban wall-clock/random calls; seeds are explicit inputs
everywhere.
cards.front:
Why is determinism a design requirement in our pipelines, and give two
enforced examples.
cards.title: Determinism discipline

cards.back:
Injecting a high-weight time_after(T) → exit transition into every state
plus a dedicated _depart exit state — a guard that bounds looping-FSM
persistence so headcount matches the scripted arm by construction. A
formal-modelling fix (add a timeout guard) to an experimental confound.
cards.front:
What runtime FSM pattern capped unbounded dwell in the reactive-crowd
arms?
cards.title: Guarded transitions in practice

cards.back:
Pydantic models (scenario configs, deck cards, GIS payloads) are machine-
checked contracts: invalid states are unrepresentable, validation errors
are caught before compute is spent (sim_scenario_validate caught both a
wrong field name and a runtime-only illegal target), and the schema doc
IS the spec.
cards.front: How do typed schemas act as lightweight formal specs in the platform?
cards.title: Schema as contract

cards.example:
The division, done on one tone. The standard fixes the training symbol, so
say X(k) = 1 + 0j. The receiver measures Y(k) = 0.30 − 0.40j. Then
Ĥ(k) = Y/X = **0.30 − 0.40j**, an amplitude of 0.50 and a phase of about
−53°.

Now note what made that trivial: the receiver knew X. That is the entire
reason CSI is free — the preamble exists so the receiver can equalise the
frame, and equalising means computing exactly this ratio, 242 times, on every
frame that arrives.

And what makes it fragile: the noise term N(k) is not in the equation you
solve. Dividing by a known symbol gives you H plus a noise-shaped error, so a
weak frame produces a confident-looking channel estimate that is mostly
noise. This is why delivery and yield are measurands rather than plumbing.
cards.explanation:
CSI is precisely the vector of recovered H(k) over the occupied
subcarriers. The receiver must estimate it to EQUALISE the symbol, so
sensing is a by-product of ordinary demodulation and costs no extra radio.
Read per subcarrier rather than aggregated: a body creates a
frequency-selective perturbation, and aggregating is exactly the operation
that destroys it. That is the one-line case for CSI over RSSI.

fields.meaning: received symbol on subcarrier k
transmitted symbol on subcarrier k
complex channel coefficient — the CSI
additive noise

figures.caption: Sensing is not an extra measurement. The receiver divides what arrived by what it knows was sent, because that is how equalisation works — and the quotient is the channel.

nodes.label: transmitter sends X(k) — a symbol BOTH ends know
it must do this to decode the frame at all

cards.question:
Write the per-subcarrier model that makes CSI exist, and say why the
receiver has already computed it.
cards.reading:
The received symbol on subcarrier k is the transmitted symbol multiplied
by the complex channel coefficient, plus noise.
cards.title: The narrowband channel model

cards.example:
Our own room, decomposed. The shelving, floor, walls and radiator never move,
so their contributions add up to one fixed complex number H₀ — that is the
certified-empty channel, and over a thousand minutes of verified-empty
observation is what makes it measurable rather than assumed.

Add one walker. Their reflection is a phasor of some amplitude a₁ whose angle
φ₁(t) turns as they move: a metre of path change at 5 GHz is about **16 full
turns** of that angle. So the sum H₀ + a₁e^{jφ₁} traces a circle of radius a₁
around the fixed point, and the amplitude |H| oscillates between |H₀| − a₁
and |H₀| + a₁.

That single picture explains why motion is easy and stillness is hard. A
moving phasor sweeps the circle and the amplitude visibly wobbles. A person
sitting still holds their angle fixed, and the sum is just another static
channel — indistinguishable from a slightly different empty room.
cards.explanation:
This is the derivation's starting point, and it is where every subsequent
result comes from. Three things follow directly. The phasors are assumed
approximately INDEPENDENT, which is what licenses a central-limit argument
at low density. H₀ sets the MEAN, which is why the mean-scaled coefficient
of variation is the natural normaliser rather than a convenience. And a
shorter wavelength gives a larger phase swing per unit body displacement,
which predicts the 5 GHz band advantage instead of measuring it
separately.

fields.meaning: static component — the room, its walls and furniture
number of independent moving scatterers (people)
scattering amplitude of the k-th mover
its phase, which varies as the body moves

figures.caption: Adding independent random phasors grows the resultant as the square root of their number — that is the central-limit half. A real room runs out of independent scatterers, and the dashed curve is what that does.

cards.question:
Model the channel as a static part plus movers. Write it, and name the
physical assumption each term carries.
cards.reading:
The channel at one subcarrier is a fixed component plus a sum of K moving
random phasors, one per person.
cards.title: The phasor decomposition

cards.example:
Put K₀ = 4 in the law and read off what each new occupant buys, as a fraction
of the saturated variance.

One occupant: 1 − e^(−0.25) = **0.22**. Two: **0.39**. Four: **0.63**.
Eight: **0.86**. Twelve: **0.95**.

So the first occupant delivers 22% of the whole dynamic range and the step
from eight to nine delivers **3%** — a factor of seven weaker. That is the
saturation, in numbers, and it is why presence detection reaches an AUC near
0.99 while graded counting in a full room is hard.

The practical reading for an operator: a system built on this law is
excellent at "is anyone there", good at "a few or many", and progressively
worse at "sixteen or nineteen" — and that ordering is a property of the
physics rather than of the estimator.
cards.explanation:
The SHAPE is derived: a central-limit argument at low density, plus a
finite room whose mutual occlusion caps the number of EFFECTIVE
independent scatterers. The SCALE K₀ is fitted — and Pillar 2a exists to
supply the mechanism behind it. On the pooled real corpus the concave form
is AIC-preferred over a line in five of seven counting-band environments,
and in every dual-band room the fitted saturation scale sits inside the
observed occupancy range, which is what makes it genuine saturation rather
than a disguised line. The trap to avoid: this is not "we saw variance
rise". It is a prediction of a model that also predicts the band
advantage.

fields.meaning: temporal fluctuation power of CSI amplitude
the saturated ceiling — the fully-diffuse variance
number of independent moving scatterers
saturation scale — the effective scatterer budget of the room

figures.caption: Concave and saturating, never linear. At K = K0 the variance has reached 1 - 1/e of its ceiling; past that, added bodies buy almost nothing. A smaller effective-scatterer budget saturates sooner.

cards.question:
State the count-to-variance law. Is its shape derived or fitted — and
which part of it is which?
cards.reading:
Amplitude variance rises with the number of movers and saturates towards a
ceiling, at a rate set by the saturation scale.
cards.title: Pillar 2 — the scattering law

cards.example:
The derivative is the operator's sensitivity curve, so evaluate it.

With K₀ = 4 the marginal variance per extra occupant is (σ²/4)e^(−K/4):
at K = 0 it is **0.25 σ²**, at K = 4 it is **0.092 σ²**, at K = 8 it is
**0.034 σ²**, at K = 12 it is **0.012 σ²**.

Read as an error budget: if the measurement noise on a window's variance is
fixed, then the count resolution degrades in exactly this ratio. Around
twelve occupants the signal per additional person is about a twentieth of
what it was at zero, so an estimator that resolves one person at low
occupancy resolves roughly twenty at high occupancy — with no bug anywhere.

This is the strongest argument in the thesis for a distributional output
contract. A point estimate hides the fact that its own resolution collapsed;
a distribution widens.
cards.explanation:
This is the single most useful consequence of the derivation, because it
answers a question the field usually treats as two separate facts.
Presence detection is nearly solved — the step from zero to one occupant
sits at maximum sensitivity, and the occupancy–variance proxy reaches an
AUC of up to 0.99. Graded counting in a full room is hard, because by then
the same feature is on the flat part of the curve. One decaying derivative
explains both. It also sets an honest expectation: no amount of estimator
cleverness recovers information the channel stopped providing.

fields.meaning: marginal sensitivity — variance gained per extra body
saturation scale
occupants already present

figures.caption: The first occupant moves the feature by the full amount. The tenth moves it by a fraction of that. Same law, plotted as its own derivative.

cards.question:
Differentiate the scattering law. What does the derivative explain about
the difference between presence detection and graded counting?
cards.reading:
The marginal variance gained per additional occupant decays exponentially
with the number already present.
cards.title: Why presence is easy and counting is hard

cards.example:
Our own window arithmetic, which turns the abstract edge into a design knob.

A 2 × 2 node on a 20 MHz HE channel has p = 4 × 242 = **968** dimensions. At
the measured 608 Hz, a **one-second** window gives n = 608, so γ ≈ 1.6 and
the noise bulk reaches (1 + √1.6)² ≈ **5.1 σ²**. A **ten-second** window
gives n = 6080, γ ≈ 0.16, and the edge falls to about **1.96 σ²**.

Same room, same people: the threshold an occupant's eigenvalue must clear
changed by a factor of 2.6 because the window changed. So a saturation knee
measured at one window length is not a property of the room, and quoting it
without p and n is quoting half a result.

The corollary is uncomfortable and worth volunteering: longer windows lower
the bar and also average over motion, so there is an optimum rather than a
monotone improvement.
cards.explanation:
Modelling occupants as perturbations of the channel covariance, the
spiked-covariance model says a perturbation produces a detached sample
eigenvalue only once its strength clears this edge; below it the
eigenvalue sticks to the bulk and the occupant is spectrally invisible.
So saturation is the regime in which added occupants fall BELOW the edge,
and the knee is a function of measurement geometry rather than of the
room. Real-hardware support exists and so does a retraction: the number of
modes above the edge tracks occupancy monotonically and concavely, and the
aspect-ratio scaling holds strictly — but the literal identity "occupancy
equals number of detached modes" fired its own refutation condition and is
retired, because occupancy is a coherent low-rank perturbation rather than
N independent spikes.

fields.meaning: upper edge of the Marchenko–Pastur noise bulk
aspect ratio of the sample covariance
antenna x subcarrier dimensions
snapshots in the capture window

figures.caption: Short windows push γ up, the edge rises, and fewer occupants clear it. The detection budget is a design variable, not a constant of the room.

cards.question:
Where does the saturation scale K₀ come from? Give the random-matrix
answer and the quantity it depends on.
cards.reading:
The noise bulk of a sample covariance ends at an upper edge fixed by the
aspect ratio; an occupant is visible only once its eigenvalue detaches
above that edge.
cards.title: Pillar 2a — the detection edge

cards.example:
Two one-second windows on the same subcarrier of the same node, in the
receiver's own units.

Empty: mean 0.500, standard deviation 0.010, **CV 0.02**. Occupied: mean
0.480, standard deviation 0.062, **CV 0.13**. The level moved 4%; the ratio
moved sixfold.

Then the failure the normaliser prevents. Let the automatic gain control step
by 1.8× during the second window: the standard deviation becomes 0.112 and
the RAW variance is now roughly 125 times the empty-room value, while the CV
is unchanged at **0.13**. A pipeline reading raw variance would have reported
a crowd that was an amplifier.

That is why the mean is in the denominator: the phasor model says the static
component sets the mean, and dividing by it is what the derivation
prescribes.
cards.explanation:
The phasor model says the static component H₀ sets the mean, so dividing
